@@ -0,0 +1,618 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Miner Sentiment Polling
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process / Ecosystem
+    Created: 2026-10-27
+    License: MIT
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document are to be
+interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear in all
+capitals.
+
+The character § is used when referring to sections of the Zcash Protocol
+Specification. [^protocol]
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in § 3.12
+‘Mainnet and Testnet’. [^protocol-networks]
+
+The terms "best valid block chain" and "block height" are to be interpreted as
+described in § 3.3 ‘The Block Chain’ [^protocol-blockchain], and the term "coinbase
+transaction" as described in § 3.11 ‘Coinbase Transactions’.
+[^protocol-coinbasetransactions]
+
+The term "network upgrade" is to be interpreted as described in ZIP 200.
+[^zip-0200]
+
+The term "Zcash Community Advisory Panel" (or "ZCAP") is to be interpreted as
+described in ZIP 1015. [^zip-1015]
+
+The terms below are to be interpreted as follows:
+
+Election
+:   A round of sentiment polling on the scope or timing of one or more upcoming
+    network upgrades, consisting of a ZCAP Poll and the Miner Poll specified in
+    this ZIP.
+
+ZCAP Poll
+:   The poll of ZCAP members held for an Election. [^nu7-poll-results]
+
+Miner Poll
+:   The poll of miners held for an Election, as specified in this ZIP.
+
+Poll Organizer
+:   The ZCAP, as the organizer of the ZCAP Poll of an Election.
+
+Poll Definition
+:   The document that specifies a Miner Poll; see [Poll Definitions].
+
+Election Identifier
+:   The short string that identifies an Election in Miner Ballots.
+
+Voting Period
+:   The inclusive range of block heights in which Miner Ballots for an Election
+    are counted, from the Voting Start Height to the Voting End Height.
+
+Miner Data
+:   The bytes of the script of the transparent input of a coinbase transaction
+    that follow the encoding of the block height required by § 7.1.2
+    ‘Transaction Consensus Rules’. [^protocol-txnconsensus]
+
+Coinbase Memo
+:   The memo field of a shielded output of a coinbase transaction, as recovered by
+    decrypting the output using a sequence of 32 zero bytes as the outgoing
+    viewing key, as specified in § 4.20.3 ‘Decryption using an Outgoing Viewing
+    Key (Sapling and Orchard)’. [^protocol-decryptovk] [^zip-0213]
+
+Miner Ballot
+:   A string that encodes a miner's answers to the questions of an Election; see
+    [Miner Ballots].
+
+Option Character
+:   A byte that is an ASCII digit `1` to `9` or an uppercase ASCII letter `A` to
+    `Z`.
+
+Answer Character
+:   A byte that is an Option Character, a hyphen `-`, or a parenthesis `(` or
+    `)`.
+
+Participation Threshold
+:   The minimum percentage of the blocks in a Voting Period that answer a
+    question, for the Miner Poll results on that question to be considered
+    representative of miners.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This proposal specifies a process for gauging miners' sentiment on upcoming
+network upgrades. For each Election, miners answer the same questions, with the
+same options, as the ZCAP.
+
+A miner votes by including a compact ASCII Miner Ballot in the coinbase
+transaction of each block it mines within a Voting Period, which the community
+agrees upon through public review and which is fixed in block heights in
+advance. The Miner Ballot goes in the Miner Data of the coinbase script or in a
+Coinbase Memo. Each block in the Voting Period is one vote, and a block without
+a valid Miner Ballot answers no question, so results are shares of all blocks in
+the Voting Period and approximate shares of hashrate. Anyone can compute them
+from the block chain.
+
+Miner Poll results are published alongside ZCAP Poll results. Miner Ballots are
+public and linked to the blocks that carry them. No consensus change is
+required.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+The scope of network upgrades is decided with input from polls of the ZCAP,
+whose NU7 results ZIP 259 cites. [^zip-0259] Coinholder polls, such as the NU7
+coinholder vote [^nu7-poll-questions], are also held, but are not officially
+recognized.
+
+Miners are not polled, although network upgrades affect them directly. NU7
+changes the block target spacing and the block subsidy per block [^zip-0218], and
+removes 60% of transaction fees from circulation [^zip-0235]. An upgrade also
+activates safely only if miners run node software that supports it.
+
+Miners already put free-form text in coinbase transactions, and ZIP 213
+anticipated identifying text in shielded coinbase memos [^zip-0213], but without
+a common format that text cannot be tallied. A common encoding makes the tally
+reproducible by anyone, and asking the questions of the ZCAP Poll makes the
+results directly comparable.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+Miner Ballots are public by design and linked to the blocks that carry them and
+to their coinbase outputs. Coinbase outputs are already public: transparent
+outputs directly, and shielded outputs because they decrypt with the all-zero
+outgoing viewing key [^zip-0213]. A Miner Ballot therefore reveals only the
+miner's answers.
+
+Unlike a ZCAP Poll, a Miner Poll has no ballot secrecy: the positions of mining
+pools and solo miners become public. A mining pool votes with its hashers' work;
+individual hashers are not identified, and their preferences are not recorded.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* Miners can answer exactly the questions of the ZCAP Poll, with exactly its
+  options.
+* Casting a Miner Ballot requires no consensus change or new transaction type.
+* Existing node software can cast Miner Ballots through string-valued
+  configuration.
+* Every block counts as a single vote.
+* Support for each option is reported as a share of all blocks in the Voting
+  Period, including blocks without a Miner Ballot.
+* The tally is fully determined by the Poll Definition and public block chain
+  data.
+* The community agrees upon the Voting Period of each Election through public
+  review, and the Voting Period is fixed in advance and unambiguous.
+* Miner Poll results are comparable with ZCAP Poll results.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* Ballot secrecy for miners.
+* A binding effect of the results, or activation signalling enforced by
+  consensus.
+* Separate representation of hashers within a mining pool.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+For each Election, the Poll Organizer MUST hold a Miner Poll on Mainnet as
+specified below.
+
+## Poll Definitions
+
+For each Election, the Poll Organizer MUST publish a Poll Definition on the Zcash
+Community Forum, in the announcement of the ZCAP Poll or in a post linked from
+it. A Poll Definition gives:
+
+* the Election Identifier;
+* the network (Mainnet or Testnet);
+* the Voting Start Height and the Voting End Height;
+* the questions, the options for each question, and the maximum number of
+  selections for each multiple-choice question;
+* the Participation Threshold, as a percentage;
+* a link to the announcement of the ZCAP Poll.
+
+The questions and options MUST be identical in wording, order, and number to
+those of the ZCAP Poll. Questions and the options of each question are numbered
+from 1 in order of appearance; an explicit "Abstain" option is an ordinary
+option. A question MUST NOT have more than 35 options.
+
+A question is single-choice if the ZCAP Poll allows selecting at most one of its
+options, and multiple-choice otherwise. The maximum number of selections of a
+multiple-choice question MUST be the number of options the ZCAP Poll allows
+selecting for it, which is from 2 to its number of options.
+
+The longest answer string of an Election has 1 character for each single-choice
+question, and the maximum number of selections plus 2 for each multiple-choice
+question. Its length MUST NOT exceed 489, so that every Miner Ballot fits in a
+512-byte Coinbase Memo.
+
+The Election Identifier MUST have 1 to 16 characters, each a lowercase ASCII
+letter `a` to `z`, an ASCII digit `0` to `9`, or a hyphen `-`. It MUST NOT equal
+the Election Identifier of any earlier Poll Definition on the same network.
+
+A published Poll Definition MUST NOT be changed. To change its questions,
+options, Voting Period, or Participation Threshold, the Poll Organizer publishes a
+new Poll Definition, which supersedes it and is subject to the requirements in
+[Voting Period]. A Poll Definition can only be superseded before the block at its
+Voting Start Height is mined, and a superseded Poll Definition is not tallied.
+Once the Voting Period of a Poll Definition has started, its Miner Poll MUST be
+tallied and its results published, even if a new Poll Definition is published
+afterward.
+
+## Voting Period
+
+The Voting Period consists of the block heights from the Voting Start Height to
+the Voting End Height inclusive. The Voting End Height MUST be greater than or
+equal to the Voting Start Height. The Voting Period of each Election is agreed
+upon as follows:
+
+1. The Poll Organizer proposes the Voting Period, together with the questions, in
+   the announcement of the ZCAP Poll and invites feedback on the forum.
+2. The proposed Voting Period SHOULD coincide with the voting window of the ZCAP
+   Poll. To convert times to block heights, the Poll Organizer SHOULD use the
+   block target spacing in effect, accounting for any network upgrade scheduled
+   to activate before the Voting End Height.
+3. After considering the feedback, the Poll Organizer publishes the final Poll
+   Definition. Its Voting Period MUST have been proposed on the forum, as in
+   step 1, at least 7 days earlier, so a Voting Period changed in response to
+   feedback is proposed again. With the final Poll Definition, the Poll
+   Organizer MUST answer on the forum each objection to the Voting Period raised
+   during the feedback period, stating how it was addressed or why it was not.
+   The final Poll Definition MUST be published at least 14 days before the
+   block at the Voting Start Height is expected to be mined.
+
+## Miner Ballots
+
+A Miner Ballot is a string of ASCII bytes with the following ABNF syntax
+[^RFC5234]. The prefix is given as bytes because quoted ABNF strings are
+case-insensitive.
+
+```abnf
+miner-ballot  = %x7A.70.6F.6C.6C.3A election-id ":" answer-string  ; "zpoll:"
+election-id   = 1*16( %x61-7A / DIGIT / "-" )
+answer-string = 1*answer
+answer        = "-" / option / "(" 1*option ")"
+option        = %x31-39 / %x41-5A
+```
+
+An Option Character selects an option: a digit `1` to `9` selects options 1 to 9
+respectively, and a letter `A` to `Z` selects options 10 to 35 respectively. The
+$i$-th answer of the answer string answers question $i$:
+
+* a single Option Character selects its option;
+* Option Characters in parentheses select each of their options;
+* a hyphen `-` leaves the question unanswered.
+
+The answer string is the longest run of Answer Characters immediately following
+`zpoll:` ‖ election-id ‖ `:`. It ends at the first byte that is not an Answer
+Character, or at the end of the containing data.
+
+A Miner Ballot is valid for an Election $E$ if and only if:
+
+* its election-id equals the Election Identifier of $E$;
+* its answer string matches `answer-string`, with exactly one answer per
+  question of $E$;
+* each answer to a single-choice question is a hyphen or a single Option
+  Character, and each answer to a multiple-choice question is a hyphen or
+  Option Characters in parentheses;
+* each answer selects only options that exist for its question;
+* the Option Characters in parentheses select options in strictly ascending
+  order, and no more options than the maximum number of selections of the
+  question;
+* at least one answer is not a hyphen.
+
+## Casting Miner Ballots
+
+A miner casts a Miner Ballot by including it in the coinbase transaction of a
+block it mines at a height within the Voting Period: in the Miner Data, in the
+Coinbase Memo of one or more shielded outputs, or in both. A Coinbase Memo that
+carries a Miner Ballot MUST be a text memo as defined in ZIP 302 [^zip-0302]: its
+first byte MUST be `0xF4` or smaller, and it MUST be valid UTF-8 after trailing
+zero bytes are stripped.
+
+The bytes of a Miner Ballot MUST be consecutive, and the byte immediately
+following it, if any, MUST NOT be an Answer Character. In the Miner Data, both
+requirements apply to the raw bytes, including script opcodes. Placing the whole
+Miner Ballot in a single data push satisfies the first requirement, and ending
+the Miner Data, or the text of a text memo before its zero padding, with the
+Miner Ballot satisfies the second.
+
+A miner SHOULD include its Miner Ballot in every block it mines during the Voting
+Period. Since each block counts separately, a miner MAY change its Miner Ballot
+during the Voting Period. A mining pool that casts Miner Ballots SHOULD publish
+its Miner Ballot to its hashers before the Voting Start Height.
+
+## Determining the Miner Ballot of a Block
+
+For an Election $E$ and a block $B$ at a height within the Voting Period of $E$,
+the Miner Ballot of $B$ for $E$ is determined as follows:
+
+1. Search the raw bytes of the Miner Data of $B$, without parsing them as script,
+   for occurrences of `zpoll:` ‖ Election Identifier of $E$ ‖ `:`. The first
+   occurrence that, together with its answer string, forms a Miner Ballot valid
+   for $E$ gives the Miner Ballot of $B$.
+2. Otherwise, search the Coinbase Memos of the shielded outputs of the coinbase
+   transaction of $B$ in the same way, in the order in which the outputs appear
+   in the transaction encoding. Skip each Coinbase Memo that is not a ZIP 302
+   text memo: one whose first byte is greater than `0xF4`, or that is not valid
+   UTF-8 after trailing zero bytes are stripped. The first Miner Ballot valid for
+   $E$ found in this order gives the Miner Ballot of $B$.
+3. Otherwise, $B$ has no Miner Ballot for $E$.
+
+Any other Miner Ballots for $E$ in $B$ have no effect.
+
+## Tallying
+
+The tally of a Miner Poll is computed over the best valid block chain of the
+network given in its Poll Definition, once that chain contains a block at height
+Voting End Height + 99, giving the block at the Voting End Height 100
+confirmations.
+
+Each block in the Voting Period counts as a single vote. Its Miner Ballot, as
+determined in [Determining the Miner Ballot of a Block], counts exactly once,
+regardless of who mined it or the value of its coinbase outputs. A block without
+a Miner Ballot for the Election counts as answering no question.
+
+Let:
+
+* $N$ be the number of blocks in the Voting Period, i.e. Voting End Height −
+  Voting Start Height + 1;
+* $P$ be the number of blocks in the Voting Period that have a Miner Ballot for
+  the Election;
+* $c_{q,o}$ be the number of those blocks whose Miner Ballot selects option $o$
+  for question $q$;
+* $A_q$ be the number of those blocks whose Miner Ballot answers question $q$.
+
+For a single-choice question, $A_q = \sum_o c_{q,o}$. A Miner Ballot can select
+several options of a multiple-choice question, so for such a question the counts
+$c_{q,o}$ can sum to more than $A_q$, and the percentages of its options to more
+than 100%.
+
+The results of the Miner Poll consist of:
+
+* for each question $q$ and option $o$, the count $c_{q,o}$ and the percentage
+  $100 \cdot c_{q,o} / N$;
+* for each question $q$, the count $N - A_q$ of blocks that do not answer $q$,
+  and the percentage $100 \cdot (N - A_q) / N$;
+* $N$, $P$, and the overall participation $100 \cdot P / N$ as a percentage;
+* for each question $q$, whether $100 \cdot A_q / N$ is at least the
+  Participation Threshold;
+* the height and hash of the block at the Voting End Height in the block chain
+  that was tallied.
+
+Percentages in the results, and in any summary of them by the Poll Organizer,
+MUST be relative to $N$. The counts are authoritative.
+
+The results on question $q$ are representative of miners if and only if
+$100 \cdot A_q / N$ is at least the Participation Threshold.
+
+## Publication of Results
+
+The Poll Organizer MUST publish the Miner Poll results in the same forum thread
+as the ZCAP Poll results, no later than 7 days after the block at height
+Voting End Height + 99 is mined.
+
+A ZIP that cites an Election's ZCAP Poll results, as ZIP 259 does for NU7
+[^zip-0259], SHOULD also cite that Election's Miner Poll results.
+
+This ZIP does not specify what weight Miner Poll results carry relative to ZCAP
+Poll results, or how the two are combined. Coinholder polls are outside its
+scope.
+
+## Testnet-specific considerations
+
+Miner Polls SHOULD be rehearsed on Testnet before the first Miner Poll on
+Mainnet. Miner Polls on Testnet are rehearsals only: they are not the Miner Poll
+of any Election and have no significance for Zcash governance.
+
+Miner Ballots have the same encoding on both networks, and Election Identifiers
+are unique only per network. A Poll Definition on Testnet that rehearses a Miner
+Poll on Mainnet SHOULD use the Election Identifier, questions, and options of
+that Mainnet Poll Definition, so that miners rehearse exactly the Miner Ballots
+they will cast on Mainnet. The 7-day and 14-day requirements in [Voting Period]
+do not apply on Testnet.
+
+## Example
+
+This subsection is non-normative.
+
+Consider a hypothetical Mainnet Election with Election Identifier `nu8` and five
+single-choice questions, which have 4, 4, 4, 3, and 4 options.
+
+The 15-byte Miner Ballot `zpoll:nu8:2311-` selects option 2 for question 1,
+option 3 for question 2, and option 1 for questions 3 and 4; it leaves question 5
+unanswered. A miner placing it in the Miner Data of a block at height 3,600,000
+can use the 20-byte coinbase script `0380ee360f7a706f6c6c3a6e75383a323331312d`:
+the height encoding `0380ee36`, the push opcode `0f`, and the Miner Ballot. As a
+Coinbase Memo, the Miner Ballot is its 15 bytes followed by 497 zero bytes. The
+same 15 bytes followed by `0xFF` and 496 zero bytes are not valid UTF-8, so that
+memo is not a text memo and carries no Miner Ballot.
+
+If the Voting Period has 100,000 blocks and only 10, all mined by one pool, carry
+`zpoll:nu8:2311-`, option 2 of question 1 has 10 votes (0.01%) and 99,990 blocks
+(99.99%) do not answer question 1. Question 1 is answered in only 0.01% of the
+Voting Period, so its results are not representative of miners unless the
+Participation Threshold is at most 0.01%.
+
+If instead 99,990 blocks carry `zpoll:nu8:2311-` and 10 carry `zpoll:nu8:23113`,
+overall participation is 100% and questions 1 to 4 are each answered in 100% of
+the Voting Period. Question 5, however, is answered in only 0.01%, so its results
+are not representative of miners unless the Participation Threshold is at most
+0.01%.
+
+The following table shows how Miner Data is interpreted for this Election:
+
+| Data | Result |
+|------|--------|
+| `zpoll:nu8:2311-` | Valid, as above. |
+| `/ExamplePool/ zpoll:nu8:2311-` | Valid. |
+| `zpoll:nu8:2311-/ExamplePool/` | Valid; `/` ends the answer string. |
+| `zpoll:nu8:9 zpoll:nu8:2311-` | Valid; the first occurrence is invalid, so the second counts. |
+| `zpoll:nu8:2311` | Invalid: four answers for five questions. |
+| `zpoll:nu8:2311-X` | Invalid: the answer string has six answers. |
+| `zpoll:nu8:2311-(ExamplePool)` | Invalid: `(` and `E` are Answer Characters, so the answer string is `2311-(E`. |
+| `zpoll:nu8:2314-` | Invalid: question 4 has no option 4. |
+| `zpoll:nu8:-----` | Invalid: no question is answered. |
+| `ZPOLL:nu8:2311-` | Not a Miner Ballot: the prefix is case-sensitive. |
+| `zpoll:nu7:2311-` | Not a Miner Ballot for `nu8`. |
+
+Consider also a hypothetical Election with Election Identifier `devfund` and two
+questions: a multiple-choice question with 6 options and at most 3 selections,
+and a single-choice question with 3 options. Its longest answer string has 5 + 1
+= 6 characters.
+
+| Data | Result |
+|------|--------|
+| `zpoll:devfund:(135)2` | Valid: options 1, 3, and 5 for question 1, and option 2 for question 2. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:(3)-` | Valid: option 3 for question 1; question 2 is unanswered. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:3-` | Invalid: an answer to a multiple-choice question needs parentheses. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:(1)(2)` | Invalid: question 2 is single-choice. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:()2` | Invalid: parentheses enclose no option. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:(1356)2` | Invalid: four selections for question 1. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:(31)2` | Invalid: options not in ascending order. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:(33)2` | Invalid: option 3 is selected twice. |
+| `zpoll:devfund:(17)2` | Invalid: question 1 has no option 7. |
+
+If a Voting Period of 100 blocks has 30 blocks that carry `zpoll:devfund:(135)2`
+and 20 that carry `zpoll:devfund:(3)-`, option 3 of question 1 has 50 votes (50%),
+and options 1 and 5 have 30 votes (30%) each. Question 1 is answered in 50 blocks
+(50%), although its options have 110 votes in total.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Rationale for counting blocks
+
+The number of blocks mined approximates a miner's share of hashrate, and proof of
+work makes Sybil voting pointless, since more Miner Ballots require more work.
+Mining pools represent their hashers, who can switch pools if they disagree with
+their pool's Miner Ballot.
+
+Blocks are not weighted by coinbase output value or timestamp, which keeps the
+tally independent of transaction fees, the block subsidy, and timestamps chosen
+by miners. A change to the block target spacing within a Voting Period changes
+the number of blocks per unit of time for all miners alike, so counting blocks
+still approximates share of hashrate.
+
+Rented hashrate could buy an outcome at the cost of that hashrate, and public
+Miner Ballots make bribes verifiable; both are reasons why the results indicate
+sentiment and are not binding.
+
+## Rationale for counting blocks without Miner Ballots
+
+Percentages are relative to all blocks in the Voting Period, as the version bits
+mechanism of BIP 9 counts a block that does not signal against activation.
+[^bip-0009] Relative to Miner Ballots cast, the 10 Miner Ballots from one pool in
+the [Example] would show 100% support for their options; relative to the Voting
+Period, they show 0.01%. A miner's influence on any percentage is thus bounded by
+its share of the blocks in the Voting Period, however few other miners vote.
+
+This is possible because the electorate of a Miner Poll, the blocks in the Voting
+Period, is fully observable, as the membership of the ZCAP is. Shares among the
+blocks that answer a question follow from the published counts $c_{q,o}$ and
+$A_q$.
+
+The Participation Threshold flags low turnout. It applies to each question:
+since a Miner Ballot can leave questions unanswered, a heavily answered question
+would otherwise make the results on an unanswered question appear
+representative.
+
+The tally does not group blocks by miner, because coinbase outputs and pool tags
+are chosen by miners and do not reliably identify them.
+
+## Rationale for using coinbase transactions
+
+Only the miner of a block controls its coinbase transaction, so proof of work
+authenticates the Miner Ballot. No consensus change is needed: consensus
+constrains the Miner Data only by the height encoding, the length limit
+[^protocol-txnconsensus], and the block-level limit on signature operations
+inherited from Bitcoin, to which the ASCII bytes of a Miner Ballot contribute
+nothing; and shielded coinbase outputs are publicly decryptable [^zip-0213]. The
+Zcash Stratum protocol keeps the extra nonce in the block header nonce
+[^zip-0301], leaving room in the Miner Data.
+
+Two alternatives were rejected:
+
+* Block header version bits: consensus only requires the block version number to
+  be at least 4 [^protocol-blockheader], but a bit expresses only yes or no.
+* Separate transactions: anyone can create them, and they are not tied to block
+  production.
+
+## Rationale for the Miner Ballot encoding
+
+ASCII suits string-valued node configuration, ZIP 302 text memos, and block
+explorers. Compactness matters because the 100-byte coinbase script is shared
+with the height encoding and pool tags; the Miner Ballot `zpoll:nu8:2311-` is 15
+bytes. Positional answers need no question numbers, and a hyphen lets a miner
+skip a question that has no "Abstain" option. Parentheses let a miner answer
+multiple-choice questions, such as the candidate and Dev Fund proposal questions
+of past ZCAP Polls, while answers to single-choice questions stay one character
+long. Requiring ascending order gives each set of selected options a single
+encoding. The maximum number of selections follows the ZCAP Poll, so that the
+results of both polls remain comparable.
+
+The Election Identifier and the exact-length, option-range, and selection checks
+keep stale configurations from counting toward a later Election. Ending the
+answer string at the first byte that is not an Answer Character makes a length
+field unnecessary. The case-sensitive prefix gives the encoding a single
+canonical form; an incompatible future encoding would use a different prefix.
+
+The Miner Ballot has no network field, and Election Identifiers are unique only
+per network, so that a rehearsal on Testnet can use exactly the Miner Ballots of
+the Miner Poll on Mainnet, keeping Testnet as close to Mainnet as possible. A
+Miner Ballot counts on the network whose block carries it: a miner that copies a
+rehearsal configuration to Mainnet votes with it on Mainnet.
+
+The Miner Data is searched as raw bytes because consensus does not require it to
+be a well-formed script [^protocol-txnconsensus], and a tally that depended on
+parsing could differ between implementations that handle malformed scripts
+differently.
+
+## Rationale for the precedence of Miner Ballots
+
+The rule is deterministic, and duplicate Miner Ballots carry no penalty. The
+Miner Data is checked first because it is always present and needs no
+decryption.
+
+## Rationale for block-height Voting Periods
+
+Block heights are deterministic, whereas block timestamps are chosen by miners.
+Changes to the block target spacing are accounted for when the Voting Period is
+chosen. The 7-day feedback period and the public answers to objections make
+agreement on the Voting Period reviewable. As for the questions of the ZCAP Poll,
+that agreement is reached through public review; this ZIP does not define a
+separate vote on the Voting Period. The 14-day notice period gives mining pools
+time to reconfigure.
+
+
+# Reference implementation
+
+Miners can cast Miner Ballots with Zebra: its `mining.extra_coinbase_data` option
+places text in the Miner Data, and its `mining.miner_memo` option sets the
+Coinbase Memo of the miner's output when `mining.miner_address` has a shielded
+receiver. [^zebra-mining-config]
+
+
+# Open issues
+
+* A reference implementation of tallying.
+* ZCAP Poll questions that rank or score options, which Miner Ballots cannot
+  answer.
+* The interaction with memo bundles [^zip-0231], if they are deployed.
+
+

prs.title: Bulk synchronization: v2 protocol primitives and Block Chain Synchronization ZIP
prs.author: arya2
prs.bodyExcerpt: Recommends how nodes synchronize over the version 2 P2P protocol. The v2 protocol draft (#1344) now defines the primitives (`get-headers`/`get-blocks`/`get-hashes`) and the normative synchronization rules for both headers-first and checkpointed synchronization; this ZIP recommends concrete strategie

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,634 @@
+    ZIP: XXX
+    Title: Block Chain Synchronization
+    Owners: Arya <arya@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Network
+    Created: 2026-08-06
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/issues/352>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "MAY", and
+"RECOMMENDED" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14
+[^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in
+section 3.12 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-networks]
+
+The term "block chain" in this document is to be interpreted as described in
+section 3.3 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-blockchain]
+
+The term "v2 protocol" in this document refers to the version 2 Zcash P2P
+network protocol [^draft-p2p-v2]. The terms "peer" and "request stream", the
+`get-headers`, `get-blocks`, `get-hashes`, `get-block-range`,
+`get-tree-roots`, and `get-object` request stream types, the service flags,
+and the synchronization rules of that protocol, are to be interpreted as
+defined there.
+
+best chain
+:   The best valid block chain, as described in section 3.3 of the Zcash
+    Protocol Specification [^protocol-blockchain]; its *tip* is its highest
+    block.
+
+validated tip
+:   The highest block that a node has accepted into its best chain under the
+    v2 protocol's synchronization rules.
+
+synchronization strategy
+:   A procedure by which a node advances its validated tip toward the network
+    chain tip, using the request streams of the v2 protocol.
+
+checkpoint
+:   A (height, block hash) pair that a synchronizing node treats as
+    authoritative for the block at that height.
+
+trusted commitment
+:   As defined in the v2 protocol's checkpointed synchronization rules
+    [^draft-p2p-v2]; extended in this ZIP to also bind, for snapshot
+    synchronization, a state snapshot manifest.
+
+synchronization artifact
+:   The immutable, content-addressed byte object served via `get-object`, as
+    defined in the v2 protocol [^draft-p2p-v2] — for example, a known-hash
+    chunk file or a snapshot piece.
+
+known-hash list
+:   The block hashes of every height of a span of the chain, together with
+    per-block sync-cost metadata, bound by a trusted commitment (for
+    example, as the pinned hashes of a list of chunk artifacts).
+
+anchor
+:   The anchor of a `get-block-range` stream, as defined in the v2 protocol
+    [^draft-p2p-v2]; in this ZIP, always a block hash verified against a
+    trusted commitment (directly, or via a verified artifact).
+
+work unit
+:   A contiguous range of blocks (or a byte range of an artifact) scheduled
+    for download as one request stream.
+
+snapshot
+:   A serialization of a node's chain state at a *snapshot height* `H`,
+    divided into a *manifest* and content-addressed *pieces*, allowing a new
+    node to begin operating at height `H` without downloading or validating
+    the chain below it.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP recommends how a node synchronizes the block chain over the version
+2 Zcash P2P network protocol. The v2 protocol defines the synchronization
+primitives and the rules that any use of them must satisfy; this ZIP
+recommends concrete *synchronization strategies* satisfying those rules —
+headers-first synchronization, *checkpointed synchronization* over anchored
+block-range streams, optionally accelerated by verified note commitment
+tree roots, and *snapshot synchronization*, which makes a new node
+operational in minutes — together with a download scheduling discipline and
+the policy for selecting between the strategies.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+The v2 protocol [^draft-p2p-v2] deliberately specifies synchronization
+primitives, the rules constraining their use, and only one baseline
+procedure — headers-first synchronization. This ZIP recommends the concrete
+procedures, because the difference between a naive procedure and a good one
+is measured in days.
+
+Three costs dominate initial synchronization, in ascending order of what
+removing them is worth:
+
+1. **Round trips and scheduling.** The legacy protocol transferred blocks in
+   small per-request batches against individually requested hashes; at
+   typical peer round-trip times this bounds throughput at a few hundred
+   small blocks per second regardless of bandwidth. The v2 protocol's
+   `get-block-range` removes the round trip from the inner loop: blocks
+   stream continuously against a single verified anchor, and per-block
+   download handles are unnecessary.
+
+2. **Validation CPU.** Under checkpointed synchronization, proofs and
+   signatures below the final checkpoint are vouched for by the trusted
+   commitment, and the dominant remaining CPU cost — measured at roughly
+   70% of block-commit time in the Zebra implementation — is recomputing
+   the note commitment trees, leaf by leaf, only to learn per-block roots
+   that are already bound by header commitments. Verified tree roots
+   (`get-tree-roots`) eliminate that recomputation without adding trust.
+
+3. **The historical data itself.** A new node operator's goal is a node at
+   the tip; the chain's full history — hundreds of gigabytes — is the
+   overwhelming share of bytes and time, and most operators need it only
+   eventually (to serve peers) or never (pruned operation). Snapshot
+   synchronization removes it from the critical path entirely: the node
+   installs a verified state snapshot at a recent height and is operational
+   in minutes, backfilling history in the background if it chooses.
+
+Checkpoints themselves also motivate this machinery. The Zebra
+implementation compiles in known-hash lists covering every block — over 100
+MB of hashes that grow with the chain — because the legacy protocol offered
+no way to fetch and verify them. Under this ZIP, a binary compiles in only
+the expected hashes of the list itself, chunked by height range (a few
+kilobytes); the full known-hash list is then obtained verifiably from the
+P2P network with `get-hashes`, as specified in
+[Synchronization Data](#synchronizationdata).
+
+
+# Specification
+
+The synchronization rules of the v2 protocol [^draft-p2p-v2] apply to every
+strategy below and are not restated here.
+
+## Synchronization Data
+
+A node's trusted commitment binds the data its strategies rely on:
+
+- **Known-hash lists**, as pinned SHA-256 hashes of the list's *chunks*:
+  each chunk is the canonical serialization of the `get-hashes` entries
+  for a fixed height range. A node obtains the entries from its peers with
+  `get-hashes` and verifies them by reassembling each chunk and comparing
+  its hash against the commitment. The same bytes MAY instead be obtained
+  as chunk artifacts from any source — bundled with the release,
+  `get-object` requests to `NODE_SYNC_ARTIFACTS` peers, or out-of-band
+  mirrors — accepted only if their hashes match the commitment. A
+  verified known-hash list makes every listed hash an anchor, and its span
+  metadata gives per-height sizes and costs for scheduling.
+
+  The commitment MAY additionally bind a single SHA-256 hash of the
+  *spentness hints*: the hint bits for every transparent output created
+  at or below the final checkpoint (see
+  [Spentness Hints](#spentnesshints)), serialized in canonical order,
+  obtained like any artifact and verified whole against this hash. The
+  hints are committed separately from the entry chunks — one hash rather
+  than one per range — because they are a function of the final
+  checkpoint height as well as of the chain: extending the commitment's
+  coverage would change every per-range hint hash anyway, while the
+  entry-chunk hashes stay stable. A commitment from an older release
+  simply covers a lower final checkpoint: its hints remain valid for that
+  shorter span, and the node synchronizes above it normally.
+- **A snapshot manifest hash**, for snapshot synchronization (see
+  [Snapshot Synchronization](#snapshotsynchronization)).
+
+Chunk artifacts are deterministic functions of the chain, so any node that
+has synchronized the covered span can regenerate them byte-identically and
+serve them; artifact pieces SHOULD be no larger than the `get-object`
+per-request maximum [^draft-p2p-v2] so each piece is independently fetchable
+and verifiable.
+
+## Recommended Strategies
+
+A node implements headers-first synchronization (the v2 protocol's fallback
+rule requires it) and MAY implement the others.
+
+### Headers-First Synchronization
+
+Headers-first synchronization is specified in the v2 protocol
+[^draft-p2p-v2], where it is characterized as the baseline, full-validation
+method. It is also the strategy for the chain near the tip, above the reach
+of commitments, whatever strategy covered the history below.
+
+### Checkpointed Synchronization
+
+A node MAY synchronize the span of the block chain covered by a verified
+known-hash list as follows:
+
+1. **Obtain and verify the known-hash list** for the target span (see
+   [Synchronization Data](#synchronizationdata)).
+
+2. **Partition the span into work units**: contiguous block ranges, sized
+   using the span metadata toward a byte target (see
+   [Download Scheduling](#downloadscheduling)), each ending at a listed
+   height. Any listed hash can end a unit, so unit boundaries are chosen
+   freely — by bytes, not by a fixed block count — and each unit's
+   request carries the byte target as its `max_bytes` bound.
+
+3. **Stream each unit with `get-block-range`**, anchored at the unit's
+   final hash. Each delivered block is verified on arrival under the v2
+   protocol's `get-block-range` delivery rules [^draft-p2p-v2] and — as a
+   cross-check — matched against the known-hash list at its height. A
+   truncated or cancelled unit keeps its verified prefix, and the
+   remainder is re-requested from any peer, anchored at the next expected
+   hash, as the v2 protocol's `get-block-range` truncation rules provide.
+
+4. **Commit** each completed range in height order, applying whatever
+   abbreviated validation local policy permits for
+   checkpoint-authenticated blocks under the v2 protocol's validated
+   advancement rule — with tree work eliminated where
+   [Verified Tree Roots](#verifiedtreeroots) are available.
+
+A node with a commitment that binds only spaced checkpoint hashes (rather
+than a full known-hash list) applies the same procedure with units
+anchored at checkpoint heights; interior per-block cross-checks and
+advance sizing are then unavailable, but neither is needed — steps 2 and 3
+already bound each unit in bytes and authenticate every delivered block
+against its anchor.
+
+### Verified Tree Roots
+
+A node MAY avoid the note commitment tree recomputation that dominates the
+CPU cost of committing checkpoint-authenticated blocks (see
+[Motivation](#motivation)) by obtaining each historical block's tree roots
+with `get-tree-roots` from `NODE_TREE_ROOTS` peers and verifying them
+against header commitments:
+
+1. For each block in the span, obtain the entry (Sapling, Orchard, and
+   Ironwood roots, shielded transaction counts, and authorizing data
+   commitment), anchoring each request's `final_hash` at a hash the node
+   has already authenticated, so that entries describe known blocks
+   rather than the responder's view of a best chain.
+2. Verify the entries against headers that checkpointed synchronization has
+   authenticated. Which check applies depends on what the block's header
+   commits to at that height, which changes at Heartwood — *not* at NU5:
+
+   - **Between Sapling activation and Heartwood activation**, the fourth
+     header field (`hashFinalSaplingRoot`) is the block's Sapling note
+     commitment tree root. Each supplied Sapling root is checked directly
+     against it.
+   - **From Heartwood activation**, ZIP 221 [^zip-0221] repurposes that
+     field to carry the chain history root (`hashChainHistoryRoot`, and
+     from NU5 `hashBlockCommitments`, which binds the chain history root
+     together with the authorizing data commitment of ZIP 244
+     [^zip-0244]). A direct comparison against a note commitment tree root
+     is therefore *not* a valid check anywhere above Heartwood. The node
+     instead rebuilds the chain history tree from the supplied roots and
+     counts and checks the rebuilt values against each header. Each
+     block's header commits to the history tree containing its *parent's*
+     data, so an entry is verified only once the *following* block's
+     header has been checked against it.
+   - **Before a pool's activation** at the entry's height, the entry's
+     root field is 32 zero bytes and its count is 0, as the v2 protocol
+     requires [^draft-p2p-v2]; an entry that deviates fails verification.
+   - **A root that no header commits to** at the entry's height is not
+     verifiable by this procedure. The chain history tree leaf of ZIP 221
+     binds the Sapling and (from NU5) Orchard roots, but defines no
+     Ironwood field, so no header authenticates an Ironwood root.
+
+3. A **verified** root replaces the recomputation: the node adopts the
+   root, maintains tree *frontiers* only at strategy boundaries (where
+   full per-block validation resumes), and stores what its serving
+   obligations require. A node MUST NOT adopt a root that the procedure of
+   step 2 has not verified against an authenticated header, and MUST
+   recompute that pool's tree from the blocks' note commitments instead.
+   Two cases in particular are not verified by an entry's own arrival:
+
+   - Because verification above Heartwood runs one block behind, the
+     highest entry of a response is unverified until the entry for the
+     following block is obtained and checked against its header. A node
+     either extends the requested range by one entry or holds the highest
+     entry unadopted.
+   - Entries MAY be obtained and verified in any order, but each entry is
+     adopted only when its own check passes; an entry at the boundary of a
+     range is not adopted merely because its neighbours were.
+
+4. An entry that fails verification is discarded with a misbehavior penalty
+   (per the v2 protocol); the node falls back to recomputing that span's
+   trees locally.
+
+No additional trust is involved: every adopted root is authenticated by a
+header that is itself authenticated by the trusted commitment, and a root
+that no header authenticates is never adopted.
+
+**Frontier artifacts.** Adopting verified roots leaves the node without
+the tree *frontiers* it needs to resume appending note commitments where
+full validation begins. The trusted commitment MAY bind the hash of a
+*frontier artifact* — the serialized Sapling, Orchard, and Ironwood
+frontiers at the final checkpoint — obtained like any artifact. A
+frontier whose recomputed root matches the root verified for that height
+by the procedure above is adopted, so the binding itself carries no
+trust: a wrong frontier fails the root comparison and the node falls
+back to rebuilding that pool's tree from the span's note commitments.
+The Ironwood frontier cannot be verified this way (no header
+authenticates an Ironwood root); it is authenticated only by the
+commitment's hash, or rebuilt from the pool's note commitments — a
+bounded cost, since the pool postdates NU6.3 activation.
+
+### Spentness Hints
+
+After tree work is eliminated, the dominant remaining state cost of
+committing historical blocks is random access: looking up and deleting each
+transparent input's spent output, and inserting (and, under full
+validation, membership-testing) each revealed nullifier. Spentness hints —
+adapted from Bitcoin's SwiftSync [^swiftsync] — eliminate the random access
+and make historical commits order-independent, at the cost of a small hint
+bitmap bound by the trusted commitment, which vouches for its correctness
+exactly as it vouches for the known block hashes: the bitmap is a
+deterministic function of the chain, regenerable and auditable by any
+synchronized node, and its pinned hash is updated by each release that
+updates the checkpoints.
+Hints apply only within the reach of the trusted commitment: a node MUST
+NOT apply them above the final checkpoint.
+
+**Transparent outputs.** The spentness hints (see
+[Synchronization Data](#synchronizationdata)) carry one bit per
+transparent output created at or below the *terminal height* — the final
+checkpoint — in canonical order (by block height, then transaction index,
+then output index): whether the output is still unspent at that height.
+The `txouts` metadata of the verified entry chunks gives each height's bit
+count, so a node can check the bitmap's length before downloading any
+block bodies, and a work unit anywhere in the span can locate its first
+bit without processing the blocks below it. During the span:
+
+- An output hinted *unspent* is written to the transparent UTXO set as it
+  is created — and, during the span, never looked up or deleted.
+- An output hinted *spent* is never stored.
+- Transparent inputs perform no lookup at all.
+
+The constructed UTXO set is then exactly the set of outputs unspent at
+the terminal height, without a single random read: every output hinted
+spent is one the committed chain spends within the span, on the
+authority of the commitment.
+
+**Nullifiers.** The nullifier sets never shrink, so no hint is needed at
+all: revealed nullifiers are simply inserted as they are encountered —
+insertion is sequential-write work, not the random reads the hints exist
+to remove — and per-spend membership tests below the final checkpoint
+are vouched for by the trusted commitment. When backfilling below a
+snapshot, the reconstructed sets are compared with the snapshot's at `H`
+(see [Snapshot Synchronization](#snapshotsynchronization)).
+
+**Value pools.** No lookups are needed for value tracking either: shielded
+pool balances are sums of the blocks' value balance fields, which commute,
+and the transparent pool balance at the terminal height is the sum of the
+constructed UTXO set's amounts. These are consensus quantities: they MUST
+be accumulated with checked arithmetic that detects overflow.
+
+**What order-independence does and does not cover.** The state construction
+above reads no state written by an earlier block, so the *construction* —
+the UTXO set, the nullifier sets, and the value pool
+totals — is order-independent, and blocks and ranges MAY be verified and
+committed in any order within the span. The per-input reads and per-output
+deletes disappear entirely.
+
+Order-independence does not extend to consensus rules whose outcome is not
+a function of the terminal totals. A node applying hints MUST account for
+each of the following, either by checking it in height order or by
+recording it as covered by the trusted commitment under the v2 protocol's
+validated advancement rule:
+
+- **Non-negative pool balances at every block.** ZIP 209 [^zip-0209]
+  requires rejecting a block at which any chain value pool balance would
+  become negative. A terminal total says nothing about a running balance
+  that dips negative at an interior height and recovers; below the final
+  checkpoint this rule is among those vouched for by the trusted
+  commitment, and above it, blocks are committed in height order under
+  full validation.
+- **Coinbase maturity and the pre-NU5 shielded-coinbase rule**, which
+  depend on the creation height and coinbase status of the *spent* output
+  — exactly the lookup that hints remove. This is why hints are confined
+  to the reach of the trusted commitment, where these per-spend checks
+  are vouched for; above the final checkpoint, blocks are committed in
+  height order with the lookups performed.
+
+A node SHOULD obtain and verify the hint bitmap — its hash against the
+commitment, and its bit count against the span's transparent output
+total, summed from the verified entry chunks' `txouts` metadata — before
+processing any block bodies with hints, so that an unavailable or
+malformed bitmap costs nothing but its fetch; a bitmap that fails either
+check is discarded and the span is synchronized without hints. A
+published bitmap that is wrong despite matching its pinned hash is a
+defect of the commitment itself, exactly as a wrong checkpoint hash would
+be; because the bitmap is deterministic, publishers and third parties can
+regenerate and cross-check it, and release processes SHOULD do so.
+
+### Snapshot Synchronization
+
+A node with no chain state MAY become operational at a *snapshot height*
+`H` in minutes, deferring or omitting the history below it:
+
+1. **Obtain the manifest** whose SHA-256 hash is bound by the trusted
+   commitment, from any source (`get-object`, mirrors, bundled). The
+   manifest lists the snapshot's content-addressed pieces and their sizes.
+2. **Fetch and verify the pieces** from
+   `NODE_SYNC_ARTIFACTS` peers via `get-object` and/or out-of-band mirrors,
+   scheduling them like any other work units (see
+   [Download Scheduling](#downloadscheduling)); a piece is accepted only if
+   its hash matches the manifest.
+3. **Verify the state against the chain where possible.** The snapshot
+   contains, at minimum: the transparent UTXO set; the Sprout, Sapling,
+   Orchard, and Ironwood nullifier sets; the note commitment tree frontiers
+   of each pool; the chain history tree; and the chain value pool
+   balances, which the node needs as the starting point for the
+   pool-balance consensus rules above `H`.
+   The parts that the chain commits to — the Sapling, Orchard, and Ironwood
+   frontiers (via their header-committed roots) and the chain history tree
+   (via `hashBlockCommitments` of the following block, ZIP 221 [^zip-0221])
+   — MUST be verified against headers authenticated by the trusted
+   commitment. Because the chain history tree at `H` is committed by the
+   *following* block's header, the trusted commitment MUST authenticate
+   the header at height `H + 1` for that verification to be possible; a
+   commitment that stops at `H` leaves the chain history tree unverified,
+   and the node MUST treat it as an uncommitted component. The parts the
+   chain does not commit to (the transparent UTXO set, the nullifier sets,
+   the Sprout tree, and the chain value pool balances) are authenticated
+   solely by the manifest commitment, which therefore carries the same
+   trust as the node's binary — the trust model of the checkpoints
+   themselves.
+4. **Begin operating at `H`**: validate blocks above `H` under the
+   consensus rules (or checkpointed synchronization, where commitments
+   reach above `H`), participate fully in relay, and serve the blocks it
+   accumulates, advertising service flags as the v2 protocol requires of a
+   node that lacks the complete chain [^draft-p2p-v2].
+5. **Backfill in the background.** The node SHOULD backfill the history
+   below `H` using checkpointed synchronization, at low priority, and
+   advertise `NODE_NETWORK` when complete. On completion, backfill
+   reconciles the snapshot's uncommitted components against the chain the
+   node has just replayed. (The hint bitmap's bits are relative to the
+   final checkpoint rather than `H`, so backfill below a snapshot
+   proceeds without transparent hints; as background work, it is not on
+   the critical path that hints exist to shorten.)
+
+   The reconciliation discharges the snapshot's trust only to the extent
+   that each component is actually compared, so each MUST be covered
+   explicitly, and over complete entries: a comparison over outpoints
+   alone would let a fabricated or amount-inflated UTXO entry pass
+   unnoticed. Backfill therefore verifies, at `H`:
+
+   - **The transparent UTXO set**, compared as complete entries — the
+     outpoint, the value, the `scriptPubKey`, the creation height, and
+     the coinbase flag, in a canonical encoding — between the set the
+     replay constructs and the set the snapshot supplied, so that a
+     phantom outpoint, an inflated value, or an altered script is caught.
+   - **The nullifier sets**, by the same whole-value comparison per pool.
+   - **The Sprout note commitment tree**, which no header commits to, by
+     recomputing it from the JoinSplit note commitments of the replayed
+     blocks and comparing the resulting root and frontier. Sprout is a
+     closed pool of bounded size, so this is inexpensive.
+   - **The chain value pool balances**, by recomputing them over the
+     replayed span (with checked arithmetic, see
+     [Spentness Hints](#spentnesshints)) and comparing them to the
+     snapshot's.
+
+   When all four check out, the snapshot's uncommitted components have been
+   verified against the chain and the node's trust base is that of a fully
+   synchronized node. Until they do, they remain trusted on the strength of
+   the commitment. A mismatch in any of them means the snapshot was wrong:
+   the node discards it and falls back to checkpointed synchronization from
+   genesis. A node MAY instead operate indefinitely without deep history
+   (pruned operation), never advertising `NODE_NETWORK`; such a node never
+   discharges the snapshot's trust.
+
+Snapshot heights SHOULD lie at least the v2 protocol's reorganization
+margin below the network tip at the time the commitment is published, and
+snapshot artifacts SHOULD be deterministic functions of the chain state at
+`H`, so that any node of the same implementation that reaches `H` can
+regenerate and serve them. A wrong or corrupted snapshot cannot cause
+acceptance of a false state — a piece that does not match the manifest, or
+a frontier that fails header verification, is rejected and the node falls
+back to checkpointed synchronization; the commitment's only unverifiable
+claims are those with no on-chain commitment (see step 3). (This is the trust
+model of Bitcoin's assumeutxo [^assumeutxo] and of Ethereum's era archives
+[^era1], with the difference that Zcash's header commitments make the tree
+components independently verifiable.)
+
+## Download Scheduling
+
+Bulk download is a scheduling problem: divide known work across untrusted
+peers of unknown and changing capacity, so that aggregate throughput
+approaches the client's link capacity and no single peer can stall
+progress. A node SHOULD apply the following discipline to bulk transfers
+(`get-block-range` units and `get-object` pieces):
+
+- **Work units of 16–64 MiB**, realized for block ranges by the request's
+  `max_bytes` bound (with the known-hash span metadata, where available,
+  used to plan unit boundaries in advance), and for artifacts by manifest
+  piece sizes. Units near the commit frontier SHOULD be smaller, so the
+  frontier advances promptly; deep lookahead units MAY be larger.
+- **Pull-based assignment with per-peer budgets.** Maintain an estimate of
+  each peer's delivery rate (for example, an exponentially weighted moving
+  average); let each peer's connection pull the next unassigned unit
+  whenever its in-flight bytes fall below roughly 2–3 seconds of its
+  estimated rate. Fast peers thereby draw more work with no explicit
+  balancing step.
+- **Concurrency across peers.** Per-connection throughput is typically
+  bounded by a single CPU core (see the v2 protocol's bulk transfer
+  guidance [^draft-p2p-v2]); a node SHOULD download from at least 4–8
+  peers concurrently, preferring `NODE_NETWORK` peers for deep history and
+  respecting the flow control window guidance of the v2 protocol.
+- **Bounded lookahead.** In-flight plus downloaded-but-uncommitted data
+  SHOULD be bounded in bytes (a budget on the order of 256 MiB to 1 GiB),
+  not in blocks; block counts calibrated to near-tip synchronization are
+  meaningless across eras whose block sizes differ by three orders of
+  magnitude.
+- **Stall detection, twice over.** Cancel (with `CANCELLED`) and reassign a
+  unit whose peer delivers no bytes for a few seconds, falls below an
+  absolute configured rate floor, or sustains a rate far below the current
+  peer median (for example, a quarter). Cancelled block-range units keep
+  their verified prefix and are resumed per step 3 of
+  [Checkpointed Synchronization](#checkpointedsynchronization).
+- **End-game duplication.** When unassigned work runs out before the
+  fastest peers do, assign remaining units redundantly to the fastest
+  peers and cancel the losers; this bounds the tail of the download at the
+  cost of at most one duplicate unit per peer.
+- **Exact blame.** A block failing its arrival check is attributable with
+  certainty to the delivering peer, as is an artifact piece that fails
+  its hash after being delivered entirely by one peer; both are handled
+  per the v2 protocol's error and misbehavior rules, and the failed unit
+  is reassigned elsewhere. A piece assembled from ranges delivered by
+  several peers is *not* attributable when it fails its hash — the v2
+  protocol forbids assigning a penalty in that case — so the node
+  re-fetches the piece with each candidate peer serving it whole, which
+  isolates a misbehaving peer; a scheduler that assigns each piece to a
+  single peer (as the unit sizes above make natural) keeps blame exact
+  from the start.
+
+## Strategy Selection
+
+A synchronizing node SHOULD proceed as follows:
+
+1. A new node with no chain state, holding a snapshot commitment, SHOULD
+   use snapshot synchronization: it is operational after transferring the
+   snapshot (gigabytes) rather than the history (hundreds of gigabytes),
+   and no other strategy changes what the node ultimately trusts.
+2. For spans covered by known-hash commitments — backfill below a
+   snapshot, or the whole chain when no snapshot is used — it SHOULD use
+   checkpointed synchronization, with verified tree roots where peers
+   serve them and spentness hints where its commitment (or snapshot)
+   provides them.
+3. Above the reach of its commitments, and within the reorganization
+   margin of the tip, it uses headers-first synchronization.
+4. Every strategy degrades toward headers-first synchronization when its
+   prerequisites are unavailable (no artifacts obtainable, no serving
+   peers, verification failures), per the v2 protocol's fallback rule;
+   scarcity of `NODE_TREE_ROOTS` or `NODE_SYNC_ARTIFACTS` peers slows
+   synchronization but never blocks it.
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+The security properties of the strategies are analyzed in the v2 protocol's
+security considerations [^draft-p2p-v2]. All strategies here satisfy its
+synchronization rules, so the choice between them — including every
+fallback — affects performance, not the integrity of the resulting chain.
+The trust base is unchanged by acceleration: every accelerating input is
+either authenticated against the chain or bound by the trusted commitment,
+and the only data trusted without chain verification
+(the spentness hints and the snapshot's uncommitted state components)
+carries exactly the trust of
+the binary that shipped the commitment, as the checkpoints already do.
+The snapshot components' trust is discharged, for each component the
+reconciliation of
+[Snapshot Synchronization](#snapshotsynchronization) step 5 actually
+compares, when backfill completes; a node that never backfills never
+discharges it. The spentness hints stand or fall with the commitment
+itself, exactly as the checkpoint hashes do, and are auditable in the
+same way: the bitmap is a deterministic function of the chain that any
+synchronized node can regenerate and cross-check. Malicious
+synchronization data from peers produces failure, not
+fraud: every verification failure is detected and routed around, and is
+attributed and penalized where blame is provable under the v2 protocol's
+misbehavior rules. (One failure is deliberately *not* attributed: an
+assembled artifact
+piece whose ranges came from several peers — see
+[Download Scheduling](#downloadscheduling).)
+
+**Serving capacity.** Snapshot-synchronized and pruned nodes cannot serve
+deep history; if they became the majority, historical blocks and artifacts
+could become scarce. The service flags let nodes advertise what they serve,
+operators of full nodes are encouraged to retain `NODE_NETWORK` and
+`NODE_SYNC_ARTIFACTS`, and artifacts remain regenerable by any backfilled
+node and servable from out-of-band mirrors.
+
+**Fingerprinting.** The heights, ranges, and units a node requests reveal
+its implementation, configuration, and synchronization progress. This is
+comparable to the fingerprinting surface of headers-first synchronization
+and of the `user_agent` field, and carries the same mitigation: nodes
+concerned about it can align their request patterns with common
+implementations.
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+This ZIP depends on the v2 protocol [^draft-p2p-v2], which specifies the
+request streams, service flags, and synchronization rules used here. No
+version gating is required beyond the v2 protocol's own deployment: each
+primitive is refused by nodes that do not serve it, and every strategy
+degrades gracefully (see [Strategy Selection](#strategyselection)).
+Distribution can be purely in-band: the known-hash list is reassembled
+via `get-hashes`, and hint, frontier, and snapshot artifacts are served
+by `NODE_SYNC_ARTIFACTS` peers via `get-object` — which requires that
+seeders and any configured initial peers include such nodes.
+Implementations MAY additionally bundle current artifacts with releases,
+or serve them from out-of-band HTTPS mirrors interchangeably with
+`get-object` peers.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+

+
+[^protocol-blockchain]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 3.3: The Block Chain](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockchain)
+
+[^draft-p2p-v2]: [Draft ZIP: Version 2 Zcash P2P Network Protocol](draft-arya-jvff-p2p-quic-transport.md)
+
+[^zip-0209]: [ZIP 209: Prohibit Negative Shielded Chain Value Pool Balances](zip-0209.rst)
+
+[^zip-0221]: [ZIP 221: FlyClient - Consensus-Layer Changes](zip-0221.rst)
+
+[^zip-0244]: [ZIP 244: Transaction Identifier Non-Malleability](zip-0244.rst)

+

@@ -0,0 +1,386 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Compact Block Relay
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Network
+    Created: 2026-10-30
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/issues/360>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document are to
+be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in
+section 3.12 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-networks]
+
+The terms "txid", "authorizing data commitment" (denoted `auth_digest`), and
+"witnessed transaction identifier" ("wtxid") are to be interpreted as
+described in ZIP 239. [^zip-0239]
+
+best tip
+:   The tip of a node's best fully validated block chain.
+
+early relay
+:   Announcing or sending a block before the sending node has fully validated
+    it.
+
+authenticated block
+:   A block that passes the checks in [Early Relay].
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP specifies compact block relay for the Zcash peer-to-peer network,
+adapted from BIP 152. [^bip-0152] A compact block contains the block header,
+short identifiers for the block's transactions, and its coinbase transaction;
+the receiver reconstructs the block from transactions it already has. Peers
+that both opt in may also relay a block before fully validating it, once its
+header and transaction commitments have been checked.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+As in Bitcoin before BIP 152, a Zcash node announces a block only after fully
+validating it, and a peer that requests the block receives every transaction
+in it, although it has usually already received most of them through
+transaction relay. Both delay the propagation of new blocks between miners.
+
+BIP 152 replaces transactions the receiver already has with short
+identifiers, and allows a block to be relayed before it is fully validated.
+It cannot be used in Zcash unchanged: Zcash block headers include an Equihash
+solution, and since NU5 a transaction's txid does not commit to its
+authorizing data [^zip-0244], so short identifiers and the checks made before
+early relay need to cover the wtxid.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+All messages defined in this ZIP are serialized in the standard encoding for
+P2P messages. [^zip-0204]
+
+## Service Flag
+
+The service flag `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` is defined as bit 16
+(`0x0000000000010000`).
+
+A node that sets `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` in its `version` message supports the
+messages defined in this ZIP and follows the rules in [Early Relay] and
+[Peer Misbehaviour].
+
+The messages defined in this ZIP MUST NOT be sent on a connection unless both
+peers set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` in their `version` messages, and MUST NOT be
+sent before the `version`/`verack` handshake completes. Support MUST NOT be
+inferred from any other source, such as `addr` records, user agents, or
+protocol versions. A node MUST ignore these messages on other connections.
+
+## `sendcmpct`
+
+The `sendcmpct` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"sendcmpct"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 1 | `announce` | `uint8` | 1 to request `cmpctblock` announcements, 0 to stop them. |
+| 8 | `version` | `uint64` | Compact block encoding version. |
+
+This ZIP specifies version 1. A message with `announce` other than 0 or 1 is
+malformed.
+
+A node MAY send `cmpctblock` messages to a peer only while the most recent
+`sendcmpct` received from that peer has `announce` = 1 and `version` = 1. A
+`sendcmpct` with any other version disables announcements to its sender, and
+is not a protocol violation.
+
+A node MUST NOT request announcements from more than three peers at a time. It
+SHOULD request them from the peers that most recently first announced blocks
+it then added to its best chain; announcements of blocks it has not validated
+MUST NOT be counted. A node MUST ignore `cmpctblock` messages it has not
+requested. Disabling announcements MUST NOT cancel an outstanding
+`getblocktxn` request.
+
+There is no low-bandwidth mode and no compact block inventory type. Blocks
+are requested with `getdata` and `MSG_BLOCK`, as before.
+
+## `cmpctblock`
+
+The `cmpctblock` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"cmpctblock"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| varies | `header` | Block header | Encoded as in section 7.6 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-blockheader] |
+| 8 | `nonce` | `uint64` | Nonce used to compute short IDs. |
+| varies | `shortidsCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of short IDs. |
+| `6 * shortidsCount` | `shortids` | `uint8[6][]` | Short IDs of the transactions that are not prefilled, in block order. |
+| varies | `prefilledCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of prefilled transactions. |
+| varies | `prefilled` | `PrefilledTransaction[]` | Prefilled transactions, in block order. |
+
+The header includes the Equihash solution, and does not include the
+transaction count that follows it in a `headers` message. On Mainnet and
+Testnet it is 1,487 bytes.
+
+A `PrefilledTransaction` has the following format:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| varies | `index` | `CompactSize` | Differentially encoded index of the transaction in the block. |
+| varies | `tx` | Transaction | The transaction, encoded as in section 7.1 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-txnencoding] |
+
+In a list of differentially encoded indexes, the first entry is the absolute
+index, and each later entry is the absolute index minus the previous absolute
+index minus 1. For example, `[0, 0, 2]` encodes the absolute indexes
+`[0, 1, 4]`. Counts and indexes MUST be checked before allocation or
+indexing, and count addition and index decoding MUST NOT overflow.
+
+Let `n = shortidsCount + prefilledCount` be the number of transactions in the
+block. A node MUST reject a `cmpctblock` message if:
+
+- any of `shortidsCount`, `prefilledCount`, and `n` exceeds 37,037;
+- the absolute prefilled indexes are not strictly increasing, or any is not
+  less than `n`;
+- the first prefilled transaction is not a coinbase transaction at index 0,
+  or any other prefilled transaction is a coinbase transaction; or
+- the sizes of the header, the `CompactSize` encoding of `n`, and the
+  prefilled transactions, plus 54 bytes for each short ID, sum to more than
+  2,000,000 bytes.
+
+Senders SHOULD prefill only the coinbase transaction.
+
+### Short Transaction IDs
+
+The sender SHOULD choose `nonce` uniformly at random for each `cmpctblock`
+message. The short ID of a transaction is computed as follows:
+
+1. Let `h` be the SHA-256 hash of the encoded block header followed by
+   `nonce`.
+2. Let `k0` and `k1` be bytes 0 to 7 and 8 to 15 of `h`, each interpreted as
+   a little-endian `uint64`.
+3. Compute SipHash-2-4 with keys `(k0, k1)` of the transaction's 32-byte txid
+   for v4 and earlier transactions, or of its 64-byte wtxid for v5 and later
+   transactions.
+4. The short ID is the first 6 bytes of the little-endian encoding of the
+   result.
+
+## `getblocktxn` and `blocktxn`
+
+The `getblocktxn` message is defined as a message where the `command` field
+is (NUL-padded) `"getblocktxn"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 32 | `blockHash` | `uint8[32]` | Hash of the block announced by `cmpctblock`. |
+| varies | `indexesCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of requested transactions. |
+| varies | `indexes` | `CompactSize[]` | Differentially encoded indexes of the requested transactions. |
+
+The `indexesCount` field MUST NOT exceed 37,037, and the absolute indexes
+MUST be strictly increasing and less than `n`.
+
+The `blocktxn` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"blocktxn"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 32 | `blockHash` | `uint8[32]` | `blockHash` from the request. |
+| varies | `txCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of transactions. |
+| varies | `tx` | Transaction[] | The requested transactions, in the order requested. |
+
+A `blocktxn` message MUST contain exactly the requested transactions, which
+MUST NOT exceed 2,000,000 bytes in total.
+
+A node that sends a `cmpctblock` message MUST be able to answer a
+`getblocktxn` request for any subset of the block's transactions, and SHOULD
+retain the block for this purpose for 15 seconds. It SHOULD limit the
+`blocktxn` messages it sends for one `cmpctblock` message, including repeated
+and empty responses, to 2,000,000 bytes in total, and MAY ignore requests
+beyond that limit or after that time. It MUST ignore requests for blocks it
+has not announced on that connection or no longer retains, and requests for
+indexes outside the block.
+
+A node MUST ignore a `blocktxn` message that does not answer its outstanding
+`getblocktxn` request on that connection, and SHOULD wait at most two seconds
+for the answer.
+
+## Sending Compact Blocks
+
+A node MUST send each block announcement as `cmpctblock` to at most three
+peers, and SHOULD do so only when the `cmpctblock` message is smaller than the
+block. Other peers receive the announcement as before. A node MAY announce a
+fully validated block with `cmpctblock` to any peer that requested
+announcements.
+
+### Early Relay
+
+A node MAY relay a block before fully validating it only to peers that set
+`NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS`, and only after checking that:
+
+- NU5 is active at the block's height;
+- the block's parent is the node's best tip, and the block's coinbase height
+  is one more than the best tip's height;
+- the header has the expected difficulty, a valid Equihash solution, a hash
+  that meets its target, and a valid time with respect to both the local
+  clock and the median time past;
+- the block is at most 2,000,000 bytes, its first transaction is a coinbase
+  transaction, and no later transaction has a transparent input with a null
+  previous output;
+- the block passes the shielded action limits, and the subsidy and funding
+  stream checks that do not depend on value pool state;
+- the txids are distinct and reproduce `hashMerkleRoot`, and each
+  transaction's consensus branch ID is valid at the block's height;
+- the `auth_digest` values of all transactions reproduce the authorizing data
+  root, which together with the parent's chain history reproduces
+  `hashBlockCommitments`, as specified in ZIP 244; [^zip-0244] and
+- the block has not been rejected or invalidated by the node.
+
+While it completes validation, the node MAY announce the block, and MAY answer
+`getdata` requests for it from those peers. It MUST stop early relay of the
+block when its validation fails or is cancelled, or when its parent is no
+longer the best tip, and MUST check these conditions before sending each
+message. It SHOULD continue to answer `getblocktxn` requests for a
+`cmpctblock` message it has already sent.
+
+## Receiving Compact Blocks
+
+Before retaining a `cmpctblock` message or querying its mempool, a node MUST
+check the coinbase height, NU5 activation, the header's time, target, and
+proof of work, and that the block's parent is its best tip. If these checks
+fail, the node SHOULD treat the message as an announcement of the block hash.
+A node SHOULD limit the compact blocks it retains and the `getblocktxn`
+requests it sends, both per peer and in total.
+
+The node then reconstructs the block:
+
+1. Place the prefilled transactions at their indexes.
+2. For each index that is not prefilled, if its short ID occurs only once in
+   the message and exactly one mempool transaction has that short ID, place
+   that transaction at the index.
+3. If any index remains empty, send one `getblocktxn` request for all of
+   them.
+4. Check that the `blocktxn` response contains one transaction for each
+   requested index, with the corresponding short ID.
+5. Check the block size, the coinbase transaction, that the txids are
+   distinct and reproduce `hashMerkleRoot`, and that the `auth_digest` values
+   reproduce the commitments as in [Early Relay], then fully validate the
+   block.
+
+Step 5 is required because a short ID can match the wrong transaction, and
+`hashMerkleRoot` does not commit to authorizing data.
+
+If any step fails, or the response does not arrive in time, the node MUST
+request the block from the same peer with `getdata` and `MSG_BLOCK`, using its
+usual timeout. A reconstruction failure MUST NOT cause the node to treat the
+block as invalid.
+
+## Peer Misbehaviour
+
+A node MAY treat a malformed message defined in this ZIP as it treats other
+malformed P2P messages. This includes non-canonical `CompactSize` encodings,
+indexes out of range, and counts or sizes that exceed the limits above.
+
+A node MUST NOT penalize a peer for short ID collisions, failed
+reconstructions, commitment mismatches in reconstructed blocks, `blocktxn`
+timeouts, or an unknown parent.
+
+A node MUST NOT penalize a peer that set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` when an
+authenticated block it sent fails later validation; the node still rejects
+the block. A node MAY penalize a peer that sends a full block failing the
+proof of work, size, structure, or commitment checks in [Early Relay]. If the
+node cannot authenticate a block because the parent's chain history is
+unavailable, but the block passes the checks that do not depend on it, the
+node MUST NOT penalize the peer for a later transaction or contextual
+validation failure. Failures of local time policy and local invalidation are
+not peer misbehaviour.
+
+## Deployment
+
+This ZIP applies on Mainnet and Testnet from NU5 activation. It does not
+require a network upgrade. Peers that do not set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` use
+block relay as before.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+This ZIP differs from BIP 152 as follows:
+
+- The header is the Zcash block header, including the Equihash solution.
+- Short IDs are computed from the wtxid for v5 and later transactions, so
+  version 1 of the encoding is not Bitcoin's version 1.
+- Only high-bandwidth announcements are defined.
+- Support is signalled by a service flag rather than a protocol version, and
+  an unsupported version disables announcements rather than being negotiated.
+- The coinbase transaction is always prefilled, and all counts and sizes are
+  bounded.
+- Early relay requires checking authorizing data, and is limited to children
+  of the best tip.
+
+Zebra and zcashd ignore unknown P2P messages after the handshake
+[^zebra-codec] [^zcashd-messages], so a service flag is not needed to avoid
+disconnection. It is needed because both peers have to agree on the encoding,
+and on not penalizing authenticated blocks that fail later validation; an
+ignored message establishes neither. A protocol version signals support for a
+network upgrade, not for an optional relay policy. [^zip-0201]
+
+The limit of 37,037 transactions is the 2,000,000-byte block size limit
+divided by 54 bytes, a lower bound on the size of a transaction.
+
+Bit 16 avoids the service flags allocated in Zcash and Bitcoin
+[^bitcoin-services], the range 24 to 31 reserved for temporary experiments,
+and bits 12 to 14, which are used by pending Bitcoin proposals.
+[^bitcoin-utreexo] [^bitcoin-utxo-sharing]
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+A short ID identifies a transaction only probabilistically. A node that
+skipped the checks in step 5 of [Receiving Compact Blocks] could accept a
+block whose authorizing data differs from the data committed to by its
+header.
+
+An early relayed block can be invalid. Receiving one does not indicate that
+the block is valid, and nodes MUST fully validate it before accepting it.
+
+A `getblocktxn` request reveals which transactions the sender did not have,
+and the timing of announcements can reveal a node's peers. Setting
+`NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` reveals that a node supports this ZIP.
+
+
+# Reference Implementation
+
+Zebra implements this ZIP with the option `compact_block_relay`, on by
+default. [^zebra]
