@@ -0,0 +1,276 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox, and a ZCG Donation to the Network Sustainability Mechanism
+    Owners: Sean Bowe (Tachyon Group) <ewillbefull@gmail.com>
+            Zooko Wilcox (Shielded Labs) <zooko@shieldedlabs.net>
+            Jason McGee (Shielded Labs) <jason@shieldedlabs.net>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Consensus / Process
+    Created: 2026-10-29
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/future-dev-and-legal-defense-fund-zip/58611>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1428>
+    Updates: 207, 209, 214, 237, 1015, 1016
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHALL", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" in
+this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and
+only when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet", "Testnet", "block subsidy", "funding stream", "coinbase
+transaction", "chain value pool balance", and "Issued Supply" have the meanings
+given in the Zcash Protocol Specification [^protocol]; the character § refers
+to its sections.
+
+"Zcash Community Grants" ("ZCG"), the "ZCG Committee", the "Financial Privacy
+Foundation" ("FPF"), and the "Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox" have the meanings given
+in ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015].
+
+The "Network Sustainability Mechanism" ("NSM") and the "NSM Value Balance" have
+the meanings given in ZIP 237 [^zip-0237]: ZEC removed from circulation is added
+to the NSM Value Balance, and returns to circulation through future block
+subsidies.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP makes two changes.
+
+1. ZCG's 8% funding stream ends when this ZIP activates. For the rest of that
+   stream's term, the same 8% of the block subsidy goes into a new lockbox, the
+   **Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox**, which holds it for future
+   Zcash development and legal defense.
+
+2. The ZCG Committee donates 50,000 ZEC to the NSM within 30 days of this ZIP's
+   acceptance, by sending it to an address that no one can spend from. When
+   this ZIP activates, everything sent to that address is removed from
+   circulation and added to the NSM Value Balance.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+The rapid rise in the price of ZEC has enlarged the monetary value of ZCG's
+treasury to a much greater amount than ever before. This ZIP reduces the risks
+and pressure that come with large amounts of money, donates to the Network
+Sustainability Mechanism (providing increased long-term issuance), and accrues
+funds in a lockbox for future use by the Zcash community.
+
+ZCG's dashboard reports holdings of 91,452.98 ZEC and \$8,796,224, against
+\$2,417,165 of outstanding grant liabilities [^zcg-dashboard]. FPF reported
+\$4,718,359 of ZCG expenses in the first half of 2026, about \$9.4 million a
+year [^fpf-q2-2026]. The 8% stream adds another 144 ZEC a day, 52,560 ZEC a
+year; at \$1,300 per ZEC, that is about \$68 million a year, more than seven
+times ZCG's spending [^stream-scenarios].
+
+ZCG's treasury before and after the donation, at \$1,300 per ZEC
+(details [^donation-scenarios]):
+
+| | ZEC | Dollars | Value, less grant liabilities | Years of spending at 2026 levels |
+| :-- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
+| Before | 91,452.98 | \$8,796,224 | \$125.3 million | 13.3 |
+| After | 41,452.98 | \$8,796,224 | \$60.3 million | 6.4 |
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+The lockbox adds no addresses, keys, or notes. The donation is a public
+transparent payment to a published address. This ZIP leaves the privacy of
+every transaction unchanged.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Activation
+
+Let $A$ be this ZIP's activation height on a network, and $N$ that network's
+NU7 activation height; $A$ MUST be greater than $N$. Let $E$ be the end height
+of `FS_FPF_ZCG_H3` under Revision 3 of ZIP 214 [^zip-0214]: the third halving
+under ZIP 218's 25-second blocks [^zip-0218], $E = N + 3 \cdot (H_3 - N)$, where
+$H_3$ is the pre-NU7 third-halving height (4406400 on Mainnet, 4476000 on
+Testnet). With Mainnet's $N = 3543405$ [^zip-0259], $E = 6132390$. End heights
+are exclusive, as in ZIP 207 [^zip-0207].
+
+The lockbox rules below apply on a network where $A < E$; where $A \geq E$, the
+ZCG stream has already ended, and they change nothing. The NSM donation address
+rules apply from $A$ on every network.
+
+## The Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox
+
+The Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox holds funds for future Zcash
+development and legal defense. No one can spend from it until a future ZIP
+specifies how.
+
+**Funding streams.** A new revision of ZIP 214 makes these changes at $A$:
+
+* The end height of `FS_FPF_ZCG_H3` becomes $A$. Its recipient list keeps the
+  addresses for the address periods before $A$, as ZIP 207 computes them,
+  including ZIP 2008's change [^zip-2008].
+* A new funding stream, `FS_FDLDF_H3`, pays 8/100 of the block subsidy from
+  height $A$ to height $E$, to the recipient $\mathsf{FDLDF\_POOL}$ in every
+  address period.
+
+`FS_CCF_H3` and the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox are unchanged.
+
+**The recipient.** A new revision of ZIP 207 adds the recipient identifier
+$\mathsf{FDLDF\_POOL}$, which works as $\mathsf{DEFERRED\_POOL}$ does [^zip-2001]:
+a stream paid to it produces no coinbase output, and its value goes into the
+lockbox's balance instead. In § 7.8 and § 7.1.2, define
+$\mathsf{totalFDLDFOutput}(h)$ as the sum of $\mathsf{fs.Value}(h)$ over the
+streams paid to $\mathsf{FDLDF\_POOL}$ at height $h$, and add it to the coinbase
+transaction's $\mathsf{totalOutputValue}$, beside
+$\mathsf{totalDeferredOutput}(h)$.
+
+**The balance.** In § 4.17, add the lockbox's chain value pool balance,
+
+$$\mathsf{FDLDFBalance}(h) := \sum_{i=0}^{h} \mathsf{totalFDLDFOutput}(i),$$
+
+and include it in $\mathsf{IssuedSupply}(h)$. Add it to the pools of ZIP 209
+[^zip-0209], whose balances MUST be nonnegative and whose sum MUST NOT exceed
+$\mathsf{MAX\_MONEY}$. No consensus rule moves value out of it.
+
+## The NSM donation address
+
+The NSM donation address is the Mainnet P2SH address
+
+    t3QZUHYkaEQEuWosAc9HgMPKiQRdvuBPCQZ
+
+Its script hash, `41c98a140039816273e50db317422c11c2bfcc88`, is HASH160 of the
+one-byte script `6a`, `OP_RETURN`, which fails whatever a spender supplies. To
+check this, decode the address with Base58Check, confirm its version prefix
+(`1cbd`) and checksum, and compare its script hash with HASH160 of the byte
+`0x6a`. Spending from it would require a second script with the same HASH160.
+
+Let $\mathsf{DonatedValue}(h)$ be the total value of the transparent outputs in
+block $h$, in any transaction including the coinbase transaction, whose script
+is exactly the P2SH script `a91441c98a140039816273e50db317422c11c2bfcc8887`.
+From $A$ on:
+
+* A transaction MUST NOT spend an output with that script.
+* At height $A$, the value of every such output up to and including block $A$,
+  $\sum_{i=0}^{A} \mathsf{DonatedValue}(i)$, is removed from circulation; at
+  each later height $h$, $\mathsf{DonatedValue}(h)$ is. Call this amount
+  $\mathsf{NSMDonations}(h)$. In § 4.17, the transparent chain value pool
+  balance decreases by $\mathsf{NSMDonations}(h)$, and ZIP 237's list of
+  mechanisms for removal from circulation gains the source
+  $\mathsf{NSMDonations}(h)$, so that it is added to the NSM Value Balance.
+
+Anyone MAY send ZEC to the NSM donation address, and nothing sent there can be
+returned. Wallets SHOULD NOT offer it as an ordinary payment destination.
+Counts of circulating supply SHOULD exclude everything sent to it, before $A$
+as well as after.
+
+## The donation
+
+The ZCG Committee SHALL cause 50,000 ZEC of the funds it administers to be sent
+to the NSM donation address, in one or more Mainnet transactions. It SHALL do so
+as soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after the date on which this ZIP
+is accepted by the Zcash community.
+
+Since the funds ZCG administers are held by FPF, the ZCG Committee fulfills this
+obligation by directing FPF to create the transactions, as it directs FPF to
+make grant payments under ZIP 1015. Only FPF's payments count toward the
+donation.
+
+The ZCG Committee SHALL publish the transaction identifier of each such
+transaction to the Zcash community promptly after it is mined.
+
+## Changes to ZIPs 1015 and 1016
+
+In ZIP 1015's section on ZCG [^zip-1015-zcg], add: "ZCG funds MAY also be used
+for the donation to the Network Sustainability Mechanism that [this ZIP]
+specifies. That donation is not a grant."
+
+In ZIP 1016's section on ZCG [^zip-1016], end ZCG's funding stream at this
+ZIP's activation height, and state that from then until the third halving the
+same 8% goes into the Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox, as this ZIP
+specifies. In its section on the Coinholder-Controlled Fund, give the 12%
+stream's duration by `FS_CCF_H3`'s own start and end heights in ZIP 214, which
+this ZIP leaves unchanged.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+**A lockbox of its own.** The 8% is set aside, issued but locked, for future
+development and legal defense, and a future ZIP decides how it is spent. A
+separate balance keeps it apart from the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox's purpose
+and disbursement rules, and like that lockbox it needs no custodians or keys.
+
+**A donation by address.** NU7 deploys ZIP 237's NSM but no way for a
+transaction to remove ZEC from circulation directly: it deploys neither ZIP 233
+nor ZIP 234 [^zip-0233] [^zip-0259]. Sending to an address that no one can spend
+from lets the donation happen now; at $A$, it moves into the NSM, with every
+earlier payment to the address. The consensus change is small: no
+new transaction fields, address formats, or wallet changes. Payments from anyone
+count, so the address serves every donor. If ZIP 233 is deployed later, both
+mechanisms add to the same NSM Value Balance.
+
+**The donation's size.** 50,000 ZEC is about 55% of ZCG's ZEC. Anyone can check
+its payment on the chain, and ZCG keeps the rest of its treasury and its grants
+program.
+
+**Accounting.** The lockbox's balance stays in the Issued Supply. A donation
+moves value from the transparent pool to the NSM Value Balance in the same
+block. Both keep ZIP 237's invariant: in each block from NU7 on, the Issued
+Supply plus the NSM Value Balance grows by exactly the scheduled block subsidy.
+
+**Other proposals.** ZIP draft #1414 sends the 8% stream to the NSM
+[^draft-end-zcg-stream], and draft #1423 winds ZCG down [^draft-wind-down-zcg].
+Where they overlap with this ZIP, they are alternatives to it.
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+The lockbox and the NSM donation address are consensus changes, proposed for a
+network upgrade after NU7 that activates before height $E$; that upgrade's
+deployment ZIP sets $A$ for each network [^zip-0200]. The donation needs no
+network upgrade: it is due within 30 days of this ZIP's acceptance.
+
+
+# Reference implementation
+
+None yet.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification](https://zips.z.cash/protocol/protocol.pdf)
+
+[^zip-0200]: [ZIP 200: Network Upgrade Mechanism](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0200)
+
+[^zip-0207]: [ZIP 207: Funding Streams](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0207)
+
+[^zip-0209]: [ZIP 209: Prohibit Out-of-Range Chain Value Pool Balances](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0209)
+
+[^zip-0214]: [ZIP 214: Consensus rules for a Zcash Development Fund](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0214)
+
+[^zip-0218]: [ZIP 218: 25-second Block Target Spacing](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0218)
+
+[^zip-0233]: [ZIP 233: Network Sustainability Mechanism: Removing Funds From Circulation](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0233)
+
+[^zip-0237]: [ZIP 237: Network Sustainability Mechanism: Halving-Preserving Issuance](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0237)
+
+[^zip-0259]: [ZIP 259: Deployment of the NU7 Network Upgrade](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0259)
+
+[^zip-1015]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding](https://zips.z.cash/zip-1015)
+
+[^zip-1015-zcg]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding — Zcash Community Grants](https://zips.z.cash/zip-1015#zcash-community-grants-zcg)
+
+[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](https://zips.z.cash/zip-1016)
+
+[^zip-2001]: [ZIP 2001: Lockbox Funding Streams](https://zips.z.cash/zip-2001)
+
+[^zip-2008]: [ZIP 2008: Update to `FS_FPF_ZCG_H3` address list](https://zips.z.cash/zip-2008)
+
+[^draft-end-zcg-stream]: [Draft: Ending the ZCG Funding Stream in Favor of the NSM (zcash/zips#1414)](https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1414)
+
+[^draft-wind-down-zcg]: [Draft: Winding Down Zcash Community Grants (zcash/zips#1423)](https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1423)
+
+[^fpf-q2-2026]: [Financial Privacy Foundation: Q2 2026 Report, p. 5 (ZCG statistics, with total expenses for Q1 and Q2 2026)](https://9ba4718c-5c73-47c3-a024-4fc4e5278803.usrfiles.com/ugd/9ba471_0836532577dd4f0eab3cf5080820e622.pdf). Q2's total includes \$1,216,687 of Discretionary Fund usage, versus \$54,108 in Q1, so neither quarter alone indicates recurring spending.
+
+[^zcg-dashboard]: [Zcash Community Grants website](https://zcashcommunitygrants.org/) and its linked [Zcash Community Grants + Coinholder Grants Dashboard](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FQ28rDCyRW0TiNxrm3rgD8ai2KGUsXAjPieQmI1kKKg/edit?usp=sharing), accessed October 26, 2026. The recorded inputs are 91,452.98 ZEC, USD 8,796,224, and USD 2,417,165 in grant liabilities. The dashboard's block reference is 3,526,011 (October 21, 2026, 22:37:53 UTC), and the worksheet is marked “Updates required”. The figures are reported dashboard inputs and have not been independently reconciled.
+
+[^stream-scenarios]: The 8% of a 1.5625 ZEC block subsidy, at 1,152 blocks of 75 seconds a day: `0.08 * 1.5625 * 1,152 = 144` ZEC a day, `144 * 365 = 52,560` ZEC a year; at USD 1,300 per ZEC, USD 68,328,000 a year. ZIP 218's 25-second blocks, each with a third of the subsidy, leave the daily amount the same, apart from rounding. Annual spending: `(1,530,844 + 3,187,515) * 2 = 9,436,718` USD, from the Q2 2026 report.
+
+[^donation-scenarios]: From the dashboard figures above, at USD 1,300 per ZEC: before the donation, `91,452.98 * 1,300 + 8,796,224 - 2,417,165 = 125,267,933` USD; after it, `41,452.98 * 1,300 + 8,796,224 - 2,417,165 = 60,267,933` USD. Years of spending divide these by the 2026 rate of USD 9,436,718 a year. The figures assume no conversion costs and no further receipts, returns, or obligations beyond the dashboard's grant liabilities.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,677 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Wallet-to-Wallet Messaging
+    Owners: Arya <arya@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Standards / Wallet
+    Created: 2026-11-03
+    License: MIT
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/???>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only
+when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Unified Address", "Unified Viewing Key", "Receiver", "Metadata
+Item", "Typecode", "Producer", and "Consumer" are to be interpreted as defined
+in ZIP 316. [^zip-0316] An "Orchard Receiver" is a Receiver with Typecode
+$\mathtt{0x03}$.
+
+compactSize
+
+: A variable-length integer as used in the Bitcoin protocol,
+  [^Bitcoin-CompactSize] in minimal encoding, with a value of at most
+  $\mathtt{0x02000000}$.
+
+Sender wallet
+
+: The wallet that creates and deposits an Envelope.
+
+Recipient wallet
+
+: The wallet an Envelope is encrypted to.
+
+Envelope
+
+: An encrypted message, padded to a size class, as deposited in a Mailbox.
+
+Mailbox
+
+: A service that holds Envelopes for a Recipient wallet until it fetches them.
+
+Mailbox Descriptor
+
+: The data a Sender wallet needs to deposit an Envelope in a Mailbox.
+
+Transport Binding
+
+: A specification of the Mailbox operations over one anonymity network,
+  identified by a `binding_id`.
+
+Payload
+
+: The typed content carried inside an Envelope.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP specifies an off-chain channel between Zcash wallets. A Sender wallet
+that holds a Recipient wallet's Unified Address deposits an encrypted Envelope
+in a Mailbox over an anonymity network, and the Recipient wallet fetches it
+later. Neither wallet reveals its network identity to the other, and the
+Mailbox operator does not learn who sent an Envelope.
+
+Envelopes are encrypted to the Orchard Receiver of the Unified Address, using
+the Orchard key agreement with a domain-separated key derivation, so no new
+keys have to be exchanged. A new ZIP 316 Metadata Item carries the Mailbox
+Descriptor in the Unified Address. Payload types are defined for
+acknowledgements, text, ZIP 321 payment requests, and PCZTs, with codes
+reserved for FROST signing rounds and off-chain note delivery. Mailbox
+credentials are derived from the wallet seed with ZIP 32 registered key
+derivation.
+
+Anyone who holds the recipient's Orchard incoming viewing key can read its
+Envelopes, and a Mailbox Descriptor links every Unified Address that carries
+it. Transport Bindings are specified separately; Appendix A sketches one for
+the Nym mixnet. [^nym]
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+Several wallet protocols need a direct channel between wallets. Each wallet
+that wants one currently builds its own, so wallets from different vendors
+cannot talk to each other:
+
+- Multisig and hardware-signer flows pass PCZTs [^pczt] between parties.
+- FROST signing (ZIP 312 [^zip-0312]) runs over a confidential, authenticated
+  channel between the Coordinator and the signers whose mechanism ZIP 312
+  leaves out of scope. This ZIP supplies the confidential, anonymous
+  transport; a FROST payload would have to carry its own authentication.
+- Payment requests (ZIP 321 [^zip-0321]) and acknowledgements have no
+  wallet-to-wallet transport.
+- Project Tachyon [^tachyon] [^tachyon-post] proposes removing in-band secret
+  distribution from transactions, which makes an off-chain delivery channel a
+  requirement rather than an add-on.
+
+On-chain memos are the only standard channel today. ZIP 231 [^zip-0231]
+proposes to lift their 512-byte size cap, but memos would still cost fees, be
+stored by every full validator forever, and need a block confirmation per
+round, which rules out interactive protocols such as PCZT and FROST
+exchanges.
+
+ZIP 324 [^zip-0324] delegates delivery to a channel the parties already
+share, such as a secure messenger or a QR code, for the case where the sender
+has no address for the recipient. It does not help when the sender does hold
+a Unified Address, which is the case this ZIP covers.
+
+The idea is not new. Hornby's 2020 light wallet privacy review [^hornby-2020]
+lists out-of-band transaction delivery over a mixnet as an option and notes
+that scalable Zcash will need a mixnet or similar technology anyway. zips#629
+[^zips-629] suggests a mixnet plus a "private mailbox" to keep offline
+reception. The Nym × Zcash integration guide [^nym-zcash] covers routing a
+wallet's chain-sync and transaction-submission traffic through the mixnet,
+not wallet-to-wallet delivery. This ZIP fills that gap.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+**Who can read Envelopes.** Envelopes are encrypted to an Orchard Receiver, so
+anyone holding the account's Orchard incoming viewing key can decrypt them.
+That is the trust model of incoming notes, but Envelopes can carry more: a
+PCZT reveals a transaction the recipient is about to sign, including its
+outputs. Users who share incoming viewing keys with auditors or watch-only
+services should not expect Envelopes to be private from them.
+
+**Linkability.** A Mailbox Descriptor is a stable identifier. Two Unified
+Addresses that carry the same descriptor are linked to one recipient by anyone
+who sees both, which defeats diversified addresses. Unlinkable addresses
+therefore need separate mailboxes, at the cost of more credentials to derive
+and more mailboxes to fetch from. A `reply_to` address inside an Envelope has
+the same property for the sender.
+
+**Network observers and the Mailbox operator.** The anonymity network hides
+the sender's network identity from the operator and the recipient, and the
+recipient's from the sender. The operator still sees how many Envelopes a
+mailbox receives, their size classes, and when they are deposited and
+fetched. In bindings where the recipient connects to its own mailbox
+directly, as in the Nym sketch of Appendix A, the operator also learns the
+recipient's network identity unless the connection is tunnelled, for example
+over Tor. Network privacy is only as good as the anonymity set: while few
+wallets use a binding, cover traffic carries most of the weight.
+
+**Timing.** A deposit made at the same moment as a related on-chain
+broadcast, a fetch triggered by opening the app, or an immediate
+acknowledgement each leak timing that an observer can correlate with chain
+activity. The wallet behaviour rules in the specification reduce but do not
+remove this.
+
+**No sender authentication and no forward secrecy.** Envelopes do not
+authenticate their sender, so a Text payload can impersonate anyone; the
+specification forbids presenting it as coming from a named party. Envelope
+keys derive from long-lived keys, so compromise of an incoming viewing key
+exposes every Envelope the adversary has recorded, as for on-chain notes.
+
+**Denial of service.** Anyone holding a Unified Address can fill its mailbox.
+The cost falls on the mailbox's storage and the recipient's bandwidth; trial
+decryption itself is cheap. Bindings are expected to document quotas, and the
+unencrypted Envelope header lets a wallet see size classes before fetching
+bodies where a binding allows that.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+- A sender holding only a recipient's Unified Address can deliver a message
+  with no prior contact.
+- The recipient need not be online when the message is sent.
+- No long-term key material is needed beyond what the wallet derives from its
+  seed, and a wallet restored from seed can recover its mailboxes on a
+  best-effort basis.
+- Neither the Mailbox operator nor a network observer learns the sender's
+  network identity or links a sender to a recipient. The sender does not learn
+  the recipient's network identity.
+- An Envelope reveals nothing about its content beyond its size class.
+- Wallets that implement ZIP 316 but not this ZIP can still parse and pay a
+  Unified Address that carries a Mailbox Descriptor, provided the Typecode
+  registration requested in the Specification is granted.
+- The core protocol does not depend on any one network or token.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+- Sender authentication at the Envelope layer. Payload types that need it
+  carry their own.
+- Guaranteed delivery. Delivery is best-effort; protocols built on top have to
+  handle loss.
+- Forward secrecy.
+- Group messaging.
+- Hiding the recipient's network identity from its own Mailbox operator. A
+  binding may provide this, and a wallet can add Tor, but the core does not
+  require it.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Overview
+
+    Sender wallet                                        Recipient wallet
+         |                                                      ^
+         | 1. read Orchard Receiver and Mailbox                 |
+         |    Descriptor from the recipient's UA                |
+         | 2. build and encrypt the Envelope                    | 5. trial-decrypt
+         | 3. Deposit over the anonymity network                |    with ivk
+         v                                                      |
+      [ Mailbox ] -------------- 4. Fetch over the anonymity network
+
+## Mailbox Descriptors [mailbox-descriptors]
+
+A Mailbox Descriptor is encoded as:
+
+| Field            | Type                   | Description                      |
+|------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
+| `binding_id`     | `u16` (LE)             | Identifies the Transport Binding |
+| `descriptor_len` | `compactSize`          | Length of `descriptor`           |
+| `descriptor`     | `byte[descriptor_len]` | Binding-specific bytes           |
+
+Registered `binding_id` values:
+
+| `binding_id`                        | Binding                                      |
+|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
+| $\mathtt{0x0000}$                   | Reserved                                     |
+| $\mathtt{0x0001}$                   | Nym mixnet (Appendix A, non-normative)       |
+| $\mathtt{0xFF00}$–$\mathtt{0xFFFF}$ | Experimental; MUST NOT be used in production |
+
+## Unified Address Metadata Item [metadata-item]
+
+This ZIP defines a ZIP 316 Metadata Item, **Mailbox Descriptors**, with a
+Typecode in the Non-MUST-understand Metadata range $\mathtt{0xC0}$ to
+$\mathtt{0xDF}$, to be assigned by the ZIP Editors. [^zip-0316-metadata]
+
+The Item's value MUST parse as one or more Mailbox Descriptors, concatenated
+with no trailing bytes, in the recipient's order of preference. Descriptors
+with an unrecognised `binding_id` MUST be skipped, not rejected. A Sender
+wallet SHOULD use the first descriptor whose binding it supports.
+
+A Unified Address that carries this Item MUST also carry an Orchard Receiver;
+Envelopes are encrypted to that Receiver. The Item MUST NOT appear in a
+Unified Viewing Key.
+
+A Mailbox Descriptor is a stable identifier. A wallet MUST NOT put the same
+descriptor into two Unified Addresses that the user expects to be unlinkable.
+Wallets SHOULD include the Item only in addresses generated for a purpose
+that calls for messaging, and SHOULD NOT include it by default.
+
+If a binding's descriptors can go stale (for example in Appendix A, when the
+recipient changes gateway), the wallet SHOULD also set an Address Expiry Time
+Metadata Item [^zip-0316-expiry] on the address. Address Expiry Typecodes are
+MUST-understand, so such an address can only be paid by Consumers that
+implement ZIP 316 Revision 2; see [Open issues](#open-issues).
+
+### Typecode registration [typecode-registration]
+
+The ZIP 316 Typecode Registry [^zip-0316-registry] does not currently permit
+Producers to include Non-MUST-understand Metadata in any address type, and
+additions to the registry are made by 2xxx-series ZIPs. This ZIP requests the
+following row, to be applied when it reaches Proposed status:
+
+| Typecode | Description         | R0 | R2 `zu` | R2 `tu` |
+|----------|---------------------|----|---------|---------|
+| TBD      | Mailbox Descriptors | ✅ | ✅      | ✅      |
+
+The Item has no effect on transaction construction, so it meets ZIP 316's
+condition for `zu` addresses. Permitting it in Revision 0 addresses is what
+lets wallets that predate this ZIP pay the address, because Consumers ignore
+Items with Typecodes they do not recognise. If the ZIP Editors permit it only
+in Revision 2 addresses, the compatibility requirement holds only for
+Consumers that implement ZIP 316 Revision 2.
+
+## Envelope encryption [envelope-encryption]
+
+Let $(\mathsf{d}, \mathsf{pk_d})$ be the recipient's Orchard Receiver. Let
+$\mathsf{KA^{Orchard}}$ [^protocol-orchardkeyagreement],
+$\mathsf{DiversifyHash^{Orchard}}$ [^protocol-diversifyhash],
+$\mathsf{repr}_{\mathbb{P}}$ and $\mathsf{abst}_{\mathbb{P}}$
+[^protocol-pallasandvesta], and $\mathsf{ivk}$
+[^protocol-orchardkeycomponents] be as defined in the Zcash Protocol
+Specification, and let $\mathsf{LEBS2OSP}_{256}$ be used to encode Pallas
+points as 32-byte strings as in $\mathsf{KDF^{Orchard}}$.
+[^protocol-orchardkdf]
+
+The sender:
+
+1. Computes $\mathsf{g_d} = \mathsf{DiversifyHash^{Orchard}}(\mathsf{d})$.
+2. Chooses $\mathsf{esk}$ uniformly at random from
+   $\mathsf{KA^{Orchard}.Private}$. $\mathsf{esk}$ MUST NOT be reused across
+   Envelopes.
+3. Computes $\mathsf{epk} = \mathsf{KA^{Orchard}.DerivePublic}(\mathsf{esk}, \mathsf{g_d})$,
+   $\mathsf{sharedSecret} = \mathsf{KA^{Orchard}.Agree}(\mathsf{esk}, \mathsf{pk_d})$,
+   and $\mathsf{ephemeralKey} = \mathsf{LEBS2OSP}_{256}(\mathsf{repr}_{\mathbb{P}}(\mathsf{epk}))$.
+4. Derives the 32-byte key
+
+   $\hspace{2em}\mathsf{K} = \mathsf{BLAKE2b\text{-}256}(\texttt{"Zcash\_WalletMsg\_"}, \mathsf{LEBS2OSP}_{256}(\mathsf{repr}_{\mathbb{P}}(\mathsf{sharedSecret})) \,||\, \mathsf{ephemeralKey})$
+
+   This is $\mathsf{KDF^{Orchard}}$ with a different personalization, so
+   Envelope keys are domain-separated from note encryption keys even though
+   they share the key agreement.
+5. Chooses the smallest size class (see [Envelope format](#envelope-format))
+   whose padded size $N$ fits the plaintext, and pads the plaintext with zero
+   bytes to exactly $N$ bytes.
+6. Computes
+
+   $\hspace{2em}\mathsf{C} = \mathsf{IETF\_AEAD\_CHACHA20\_POLY1305.Encrypt}(\mathsf{K}, \mathsf{nonce}, \mathsf{aad}, \mathsf{plaintext})$
+   [^RFC8439]
+
+   with $\mathsf{nonce} = [\mathtt{0x00}]^{12}$ and
+   $\mathsf{aad} = \mathtt{version} \,||\, \mathtt{size\_class} \,||\, \mathsf{ephemeralKey}$.
+   The zero nonce is safe because $\mathsf{K}$ is unique to each
+   $\mathsf{esk}$.
+
+The recipient, for each Orchard incoming viewing key $\mathsf{ivk}$ it holds:
+
+1. Computes $\mathsf{epk} = \mathsf{abst}_{\mathbb{P}}(\mathsf{ephemeralKey})$
+   and rejects the Envelope if the result is $\bot$ or the identity
+   $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}$.
+2. Computes $\mathsf{sharedSecret} = \mathsf{KA^{Orchard}.Agree}(\mathsf{ivk}, \mathsf{epk})$.
+   Since $\mathsf{pk_d} = \mathsf{KA^{Orchard}.DerivePublic}(\mathsf{ivk}, \mathsf{g_d})$,
+   this equals the sender's value.
+3. Derives $\mathsf{K}$ as above and attempts decryption with the same
+   $\mathsf{aad}$. On failure, the Envelope is not for this key.
+4. Rejects the plaintext if it does not parse as described in
+   [Plaintext format](#plaintext-format), or if any padding byte is nonzero.
+5. Rejects the Envelope unless the plaintext's $\mathsf{d}$ is the
+   diversifier of an address of this account that this wallet issued either
+   with a Mailbox Descriptors Item or as a `reply_to`.
+
+A wallet processes an Envelope under the first $\mathsf{ivk}$ for which
+decryption succeeds. Steps 1 and 2 cost one point decompression and one
+scalar multiplication per Envelope and account.
+
+## Envelope format [envelope-format]
+
+| Field          | Type           | Description                                                             |
+|----------------|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| `version`      | `byte`         | $\mathtt{0x01}$                                                         |
+| `size_class`   | `byte`         | See table below                                                         |
+| `ephemeralKey` | `byte[32]`     | $\mathsf{LEBS2OSP}_{256}(\mathsf{repr}_{\mathbb{P}}(\mathsf{epk}))$     |
+| `ciphertext`   | `byte[N + 16]` | AEAD output; $N$ is set by `size_class`                                 |
+
+| `size_class`    | Padded plaintext size $N$ | Intended use              |
+|-----------------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
+| $\mathtt{0x00}$ | 2048 bytes                | Acks, URIs, short text    |
+| $\mathtt{0x01}$ | 32768 bytes               | Small PCZTs, FROST rounds |
+| $\mathtt{0x02}$ | 262144 bytes              | Large PCZTs               |
+
+Other values are reserved. Recipients MUST reject Envelopes with an unknown
+`version` or `size_class`, or whose length does not match `size_class`.
+
+## Plaintext format [plaintext-format]
+
+| Field          | Type                | Description                                                   |
+|----------------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
+| `payload_type` | `u16` (LE)          | See [Payload types](#payload-types)                           |
+| `flags`        | `byte`              | Bit 0: `ack_requested`; see below                             |
+| `d`            | `byte[11]`          | Diversifier of the Orchard Receiver the Envelope was sent to  |
+| `message_id`   | `byte[32]`          | Uniformly random                                              |
+| `in_reply_to`  | `byte[32]`          | `message_id` of the Envelope this one answers, or all zero    |
+| `expiry_time`  | `u64` (LE)          | Unix seconds; $0$ means no expiry                             |
+| `reply_len`    | `compactSize`       | Length of `reply_to`                                          |
+| `reply_to`     | `byte[reply_len]`   | A Unified Address, or empty                                   |
+| `payload_len`  | `compactSize`       | Length of `payload`                                           |
+| `payload`      | `byte[payload_len]` | Type-specific                                                 |
+| `padding`      | `byte[]`            | Zero bytes up to $N$                                          |
+
+Senders MUST set bits of `flags` other than bit 0 to $0$; recipients MUST
+ignore bits they do not recognise.
+
+`d` lets the recipient attribute the Envelope to one of its addresses without
+trusting `reply_to`, and `in_reply_to` lets protocols with several rounds
+match answers to requests.
+
+`reply_to`, if present, is the UTF-8 string encoding of a Unified Address
+[^zip-0316-encoding] whose Human-Readable Part matches the network of the
+Envelope's recipient. It MUST carry an Orchard Receiver and MAY carry a
+Mailbox Descriptors Item. A reply is encrypted to
+that Receiver. It is deposited in the mailbox named by the Item if there is
+one, or sent by a transport-level anonymous reply if the binding provides one
+(see [Mailbox operations](#mailbox-operations)); if neither is available, no
+reply is possible. A sender that wants replies without linking them to its
+other addresses SHOULD use a Unified Address and mailbox dedicated to replies.
+
+Senders SHOULD round `expiry_time` to the hour, to avoid leaking clock skew.
+
+Recipients:
+
+- MUST drop Envelopes whose `expiry_time` is nonzero and in the past.
+- MUST drop Envelopes whose `message_id` they have already processed, and
+  SHOULD remember processed `message_id`s at least until their expiry, or for
+  a wallet-chosen period when `expiry_time` is $0$.
+- MUST ignore the payload of an Envelope with an unknown `payload_type`, but
+  still record its `message_id`.
+
+## Payload types [payload-types]
+
+| `payload_type`                      | Name            | Payload                                                |
+|-------------------------------------|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
+| $\mathtt{0x0000}$                   | Reserved        | —                                                      |
+| $\mathtt{0x0001}$                   | Ack             | Empty; `in_reply_to` names the acknowledged Envelope   |
+| $\mathtt{0x0002}$                   | Text            | UTF-8 text for display to the user                     |
+| $\mathtt{0x0003}$                   | Payment request | UTF-8 ZIP 321 URI [^zip-0321]                          |
+| $\mathtt{0x0004}$                   | PCZT            | Serialized PCZT [^pczt]; format reference TBD          |
+| $\mathtt{0x0005}$                   | Reserved        | FROST round messages (ZIP 312 [^zip-0312]); format TBD |
+| $\mathtt{0x0006}$                   | Reserved        | Off-chain note delivery [^tachyon]; format TBD         |
+| $\mathtt{0xF000}$–$\mathtt{0xFFFF}$ | Experimental    | MUST NOT be used in production                         |
+
+An Ack MUST NOT set `ack_requested`.
+
+Payloads MUST NOT carry spend authority, such as spending keys or ZIP 324 URIs
+[^zip-0324], because every holder of the recipient's incoming viewing key can
+read them.
+
+Payload types that cause side effects SHOULD carry their own replay
+protection; `message_id` deduplication and `expiry_time` only bound replay.
+
+## Mailbox operations [mailbox-operations]
+
+A Transport Binding MUST provide these operations:
+
+- **Deposit**(descriptor, envelope): deliver an Envelope to the Mailbox named
+  by the descriptor.
+- **Fetch**(credential) → envelopes: retrieve held Envelopes.
+- **Delete**(credential, handles): remove fetched Envelopes, unless the
+  binding documents that Fetch removes them implicitly.
+
+A Transport Binding MUST hide the sender's network identity from the Mailbox
+operator and from the recipient, and MUST hide the recipient's network
+identity from the sender. It SHOULD hide the recipient's network identity from
+the Mailbox operator, and SHOULD resist timing correlation by a global
+passive adversary. Bindings SHOULD rate-limit Deposit and SHOULD bound the
+storage a mailbox can consume.
+
+A Transport Binding specification MUST state:
+
+- the descriptor encoding;
+- how the 64-byte mailbox key from
+  [Mailbox key derivation](#mailbox-key-derivation) is turned into the
+  binding's credentials;
+- the retention period, or how a wallet learns it;
+- per-mailbox storage quotas, if any;
+- which size classes it supports;
+- how replies work: by depositing to a `reply_to` mailbox, by a
+  transport-level anonymous reply, or both, and how long each path stays
+  usable;
+- rate limiting and cost, if any;
+- what network identity, timing, and size information each party can
+  observe.
+
+## Mailbox key derivation [mailbox-key-derivation]
+
+Mailbox credentials are derived from the wallet seed $S$ with ZIP 32
+registered key derivation [^zip-0032-registered], using
+$\mathsf{ContextString} = \texttt{"Zcash\_WalletMessaging"}$ and
+$\mathsf{ZipNumber}$ equal to the number assigned to this ZIP:
+
+- $(\mathsf{sk}_{subtree}, \mathsf{c}_{subtree}) = \mathsf{RegKD}(\mathsf{ContextString}, S, \mathsf{ZipNumber})$
+- $(\mathsf{sk}_{n}, \mathsf{c}_{n}) = \mathsf{CKDreg}((\mathsf{sk}_{subtree}, \mathsf{c}_{subtree}), \mathsf{coin\_type} + 2^{31}, [\,])$
+- $(\mathsf{sk}_{b}, \mathsf{c}_{b}) = \mathsf{CKDreg}((\mathsf{sk}_{n}, \mathsf{c}_{n}), \mathtt{binding\_id} + 2^{31}, [\,])$
+- $(\mathsf{sk}_{a}, \mathsf{c}_{a}) = \mathsf{CKDreg}((\mathsf{sk}_{b}, \mathsf{c}_{b}), \mathsf{account} + 2^{31}, [\,])$
+- $\mathsf{K}_{i} = \mathsf{derive\_child\_cryptovalue}((\mathsf{sk}_{a}, \mathsf{c}_{a}), i + 2^{31}, [\,])$
+
+where $\mathsf{coin\_type}$ is the ZIP 32 coin type of the network
+[^zip-0032-paths], so that Mainnet and Testnet mailboxes are unlinkable;
+$\mathsf{account}$ is the ZIP 32 account index of the Orchard key whose
+addresses carry the descriptor; and $i$ is a per-binding, per-account counter
+that the wallet increments for each new mailbox. $\mathsf{K}_{i}$ is 64
+bytes; each binding states how it is split into credentials.
+
+A wallet restored from seed can rebuild its credentials by scanning $i$ from
+$0$ with a gap limit, subject to the binding's own limits (for example,
+knowing which gateway each mailbox used).
+
+## Wallet behaviour [wallet-behaviour]
+
+Sending:
+
+- Wallets SHOULD NOT deposit an Envelope at the same moment as a related
+  on-chain broadcast, and SHOULD add a random delay when the use is not
+  interactive.
+- Wallets MUST NOT fall back to a direct connection to a Mailbox when the
+  binding's anonymity network is unavailable.
+
+Fetching:
+
+- Wallets SHOULD fetch on a randomized schedule that does not depend on user
+  actions, including when no message is expected.
+- Wallets SHOULD cap the bytes they fetch and trial-decrypt per Fetch.
+
+Acknowledgements:
+
+- Wallets SHOULD send an Ack only when `ack_requested` is set, and SHOULD
+  delay it by a random amount.
+
+Display:
+
+- Envelopes are not authenticated. Wallets MUST NOT present a message as
+  coming from a named party unless the payload type itself authenticates the
+  sender, and SHOULD NOT open links in Text payloads without user
+  confirmation.
+
+Viewing keys:
+
+- Wallets that export an account's incoming viewing key to a third party
+  SHOULD NOT advertise mailboxes on that account's addresses.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+**Why reuse Orchard key agreement?** It needs no new keys and no prior
+contact: any Unified Address with an Orchard Receiver is already a public
+encryption key. The cost is that incoming viewing key holders can read
+Envelopes; a dedicated messaging key in the descriptor would avoid that at
+the cost of a larger Item.
+
+**Why fixed size classes?** Exact lengths would leak payload types and
+content. Three classes keep the anonymity set per class large while still
+allowing PCZTs.
+
+**Why no ZIP 324 payload?** A sender that can use this channel already holds
+the recipient's Unified Address and can pay it on chain, and a ZIP 324 URI
+carries spend authority that every incoming viewing key holder could use.
+
+**Why a transport-agnostic core?** Tying a standard to one network and its
+token is a long-term risk. Nym is sketched first because it is live,
+packet-based, uses cover traffic, stores messages for offline clients, and
+offers sender-anonymous replies.
+
+

+
+None yet.

+# Open issues [open-issues]
+
+- Assignment of the Metadata Item Typecode, whether it is permitted in
+  Revision 0 addresses, and this ZIP's number, which the key derivation
+  depends on.
+- Whether to encrypt to a dedicated messaging key carried in the descriptor
+  instead of to the Orchard Receiver, so that incoming viewing key holders
+  cannot read Envelopes.
+- Address Expiry Items make an address unpayable by ZIP 316 Revision 0
+  Consumers, while the compatibility requirement assumes they can pay it.
+  Whether to recommend expiry, shorter-lived descriptors, or neither.
+- The cost of running one mailbox per unlinkable address, and whether wallets
+  should offer a deliberately linkable "contact" mode.
+- A stable reference for the PCZT serialization.
+- The FROST round message format and its authentication layer.
+- The off-chain note delivery format, to be aligned with Tachyon.
+- Support for Sapling-only recipients.
+- A Tor onion-service binding.
+- Whether the Nym binding in Appendix A becomes normative in this ZIP or in a
+  separate one, once its TBDs are resolved.
+

+# Appendix A: Nym transport binding (non-normative) [nym-binding]
+
+This appendix sketches a binding for the Nym mixnet so that the core protocol
+can be evaluated against a real network. It is not a complete Transport
+Binding specification: the items marked TBD have to be resolved before it can
+be made normative. `binding_id` $\mathtt{0x0001}$ is reserved for it.
+
+**Descriptor.** The 96-byte binary form of a Nym client address,
+[^nym-addressing] [^nym-recipient] laid out as follows:
+
+| Field                 | Type       | Description                       |
+|-----------------------|------------|-----------------------------------|
+| client identity key   | `byte[32]` | Ed25519 public key                |
+| client encryption key | `byte[32]` | X25519 public key                 |
+| gateway identity key  | `byte[32]` | Ed25519 public key of the gateway |
+
+**Credentials.** The first 32 bytes of $\mathsf{K}_{i}$ would be the Ed25519
+seed of the client identity key, and the last 32 bytes the X25519 secret key
+[^RFC7748] of the client encryption key. The Nym Rust SDK accepts externally
+supplied client keys through a custom key store. [^nym-sdk-keys]
+
+**Deposit.** The sender sends the Envelope as a Nym message to the
+descriptor's address through the mixnet, from an ephemeral Nym client with
+fresh keys rather than from its own mailbox client, attaching reply SURBs
+[^nym-surbs] if it expects a prompt reply. Each ephemeral client has to
+register with an entry gateway and hold bandwidth credentials; the cost and
+latency of doing so per message are unverified (TBD).
+
+**Fetch.** The recipient runs a Nym client with the derived keys, connected to
+the gateway named in the descriptor, with cover traffic on. The gateway stores
+messages while the client is offline and delivers them when it connects.
+[^nym-addressing]
+
+**Delete.** Implicit on delivery by the gateway (TBD: confirm).
+
+**Retention.** Not documented by Nym (TBD).
+
+**Size classes.** All. Nym splits a message into fixed-size Sphinx packets,
+so larger classes take more packets and leave a larger timing footprint.
+
+**Replies.** SURB reply keys expire after 24 hours, [^nym-surbs] so SURBs
+serve interactive exchanges only. A recipient that fetches later can reply
+only to a `reply_to` address that carries a Nym descriptor.
+
+**Rate limiting and cost.** Sending through Nym consumes bandwidth
+credentials. Who pays, and whether they can be bought with shielded ZEC, is
+TBD.
+
+**Gateway changes.** The gateway is part of the descriptor. If the recipient
+moves gateway, old descriptors stop working and a new Unified Address has to
+be issued. How a wallet restored from seed learns which gateway each mailbox
+index used is TBD.
+
+**Observability.** The recipient's gateway, which is the Mailbox operator,
+sees the recipient's connection, including its IP address unless the
+connection is tunnelled over Tor, and the count and size of stored messages.
+The sender's entry gateway sees the sender's IP address but not the
+destination. Mix nodes see packets only. A global passive adversary faces
+Nym's mixing delays and cover traffic.
+
+

prs.title: Add draft ZIP: Lock-weighted Coinholder Polling
prs.author: arya2
prs.bodyExcerpt: Draft ZIP, Process category, Status: Draft. Proposes that coinholder polls weight each ballot by how long the voter's ZEC is locked past the snapshot, not only by how much ZEC they hold. Weight is linear in lock length up to a cap of one halving interval; unlocked coins keep a floor weight of one te

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,400 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Lock-weighted Coinholder Polling
+    Owners: Arya <arya@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-03
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <URL TBD>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only
+when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" in this document are to be interpreted as
+defined in the Zcash protocol specification [^protocol-networks].
+
+The term "*Ironwood pool*" is to be interpreted as described in ZIP 229
+[^zip-0229].
+
+The terms "Coinholder-Controlled Fund" and "Key-Holder Organizations" are to be
+interpreted as described in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016]. The term "Deferred Dev Fund
+Lockbox" is to be interpreted as described in ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015].
+
+Poll
+
+: A vote in which each ballot carries a ZEC amount.
+
+Poll operator
+
+: Whoever announces a poll, verifies ballots, and publishes results.
+
+Snapshot height
+
+: The block height $S$ at which holdings are measured.
+
+Close height
+
+: The height $C$ of the last block in which a ballot can be accepted.
+
+Lock record
+
+: A triple $(v, u, c)$: a value $v$ in zatoshi, an unlock height $u$ at or
+  before which consensus forbids spending it ($u = 0$ if unlocked), and an
+  evidence class $c$. Its lock length is $\ell = \max(0, u - S)$ blocks.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+Coinholder polls count one ZEC as one vote at a snapshot height, and coins may
+be moved right after the snapshot. This ZIP changes only the weighting: a
+ballot's weight rises linearly with how long its coins stay locked past the
+snapshot, up to a cap of one halving interval; unlocked coins keep a small
+floor weight. One evidence class works today: transparent outputs locked
+with `OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY`. A second class for shielded locks is reserved
+for a consensus ZIP. Quorum and the ZIP 1016 participation threshold stay in
+unweighted ZEC. The transparent class reveals the voter's output, amount, and
+unlock height on chain, which the current shielded polling path does not; the
+shielded class is the intended end state.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+Coinholder polling gives holders a voice alongside developers, users, and
+miners. ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016] makes it the deciding input for the
+Coinholder-Controlled Fund, and about 2.4 million of 3.6 million eligible ZEC
+voted in the NU7 scope poll of September 2026 [^coindesk-nu7].
+
+The status quo is one ZEC, one vote, at a snapshot, with coins movable the
+moment the snapshot passes [^forum-nu7-vote]. Someone who buys the week of
+the vote and sells the week after is not a holder; they are renting a vote.
+This ZIP favours people credibly in it for the long haul. Someone willing to
+lock ZEC for years should have a big say, not the only say. A whale who locks
+for years still gets a big vote; they have put their coins where their vote
+is. The change removes the cheap vote, not the big one.
+
+## Scope decision
+
+There is no timelock for shielded notes. Transparent outputs can be locked
+with `OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY` [^bip-0065], which Zebra enforces on every
+transparent input [^zebra-script] `[VERIFY: enforced by zcashd since
+genesis]`. Sapling, Orchard, and Ironwood notes have no script and no lock
+field, and a transaction's `lock_time` is ignored when no transparent input
+has a non-final sequence number [^zebra-locktime], so it cannot lock a
+shielded-only spend. Three options were considered:
+
+1. A process-only ZIP using transparent locks. It works at the protocol
+   level, not the tooling level: the live mechanism accepts only notes in the
+   *Ironwood pool* [^zcashlabs-voting]. It asks holders to unshield for full
+   weight, which is at odds with the point of Zcash. Not acceptable as the
+   only option.
+2. A consensus ZIP adding a lock to shielded notes. The smallest version is a
+   lock-height field in the Ironwood note commitment, one circuit constraint,
+   and one consensus rule (see [Class S]). That is a new circuit version for a
+   pool created, with formal verification, after the Orchard soundness
+   vulnerability [^zip-0229]. It is not small and needs a network upgrade.
+3. Two ZIPs: this process ZIP, defining weighting over any lock the protocol
+   can prove, with the transparent class as an interim, plus a later consensus
+   ZIP for shielded locks.
+
+Option 3 is chosen. Everything below is defined over lock records, so the
+shielded class can be added without rewriting this ZIP.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+Under the live mechanism, validators learn neither who voted nor how much ZEC
+a ballot carried; amounts are encrypted and only totals are decrypted
+[^zcashlabs-voting]. A ballot under [Class T] reveals an output, its value,
+and its unlock height on chain to everyone, and links the ballot to that
+output unless the operator encrypts ballot contents. A voter who unshields to
+lock also reveals the unshielding transaction. That cost is why Class S is the
+intended end state.
+
+The shielded class is required to reveal no more than the current shielded
+path: the lock length stays a private witness, the multiplier is applied
+inside the proof, and locked notes are indistinguishable from unlocked notes
+on chain, including when spent.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* A ballot's weight depends on both the amount of ZEC and how long it is
+  locked past the snapshot.
+* Borrowing, hedging, or splitting to gain weight costs more than under
+  amount-only weighting.
+* Weighting is defined over an abstract lock record, so shielded locks can be
+  added without changing the rules.
+* The shielded class reveals no more than the current shielded polling path.
+* Coins with no holder, such as protocol-level lockboxes, cannot be voted.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not change who is eligible to vote, what polls are held, or
+  what polls decide. It changes weighting only.
+* It does not propose on-chain binding governance. Polls remain what ZIP 1016
+  says they are.
+* It does not change mining, block subsidy, or funding streams.
+* It does not verify custody.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Parameters
+
+$S$ and $C$ are chosen by the poll operator per poll. The floor is
+$f = 1/10$. The cap $L$ is the halving interval in effect at height $S$:
+$\mathsf{PostBlossomHalvingInterval} = 1{,}680{,}000$ blocks before NU7
+activation and $\mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval} = 5{,}040{,}000$ blocks from
+NU7 activation [^zip-0218]. Both are about four years.
+
+## Weight function
+
+For a lock record $(v, u, c)$ with lock length $\ell = \max(0, u - S)$:
+
+$$m(\ell) = f + (1 - f) \cdot \frac{\min(\ell, L)}{L}, \qquad w = v \cdot m(\ell)$$
+
+If $u \leq C$, the record MUST be counted as unlocked ($\ell = 0$). A ballot's
+weight is the sum of $w$ over its lock records.
+
+| $\ell / L$ | $m(\ell)$ | at the four-year cap |
+|-----------:|----------:|----------------------|
+| 0          | 0.100     | unlocked             |
+| 1/16       | 0.156     | 3 months             |
+| 1/8        | 0.213     | 6 months             |
+| 1/4        | 0.325     | 1 year               |
+| 1/2        | 0.550     | 2 years              |
+| 1 or more  | 1.000     | 4 years or more      |
+
+## Lock records
+
+An operator MUST accept Class H and at least one lock class, and MUST reject
+any ballot whose evidence fails verification; a failed record MUST NOT be
+counted under Class H.
+
+### Class H
+
+Class H evidence is whatever proof of holding at $S$ the operator already
+accepts, such as a proof of unspent Ironwood notes. It yields $(v, 0,
+\mathrm{H})$ and counts at the floor.
+
+### Class T
+
+Class T evidence is a transparent output whose `scriptPubKey` is a
+pay-to-script-hash of the redeem script
+
+    <u> OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY OP_DROP <pubkey> OP_CHECKSIG
+
+where `<u>` is a minimally encoded script number with
+$1 \leq u < 500{,}000{,}000$ (a block height, not a Unix time) [^bip-0065].
+The ballot carries the outpoint, the redeem script, and an ECDSA signature
+over secp256k1 by `pubkey`, as for `OP_CHECKSIG`, over a message $M$ defined
+by the operator. $M$ MUST include a poll identifier and MUST bind the ballot
+contents or a commitment to them.
+
+The operator MUST check that:
+
+1. the output exists and is unspent in the chain state at height $S$;
+2. the `scriptPubKey` equals the P2SH encoding of the supplied redeem script;
+3. the redeem script matches the template and $u$ is in height form;
+4. the signature is valid for `pubkey` over $M$;
+5. the outpoint has not been used in another ballot of this poll.
+
+The lock record is $(v, u, \mathrm{T})$ with $v$ the output's value.
+Operators MAY also accept an `OP_CHECKMULTISIG` variant of the template with
+$m$ valid signatures.
+
+### Class S
+
+Class S, shielded locks, is reserved for a consensus ZIP. That ZIP MUST
+provide: a way to fix an unlock height at note creation that consensus
+enforces on spends; a proof usable within the operator's shielded path that
+yields a lock record for notes unspent at $S$, with the multiplier applied
+inside the proof; and locked notes indistinguishable from unlocked notes on
+chain, including when spent.
+
+The smallest design known: a lock-height field inside the
+Ironwood note commitment (zero for none); a circuit constraint that the field
+is at most a per-bundle minimum height; a consensus rule that a transaction
+with a non-zero minimum height is invalid in any block below it; and wallets
+that set that value on every transaction so locked spends do not stand out.
+`[VERIFY: fit with ZIP 229 and the Ironwood circuit]`
+
+## Counting
+
+For each option the operator MUST compute the weighted total $W$, the sum of
+ballot weights, and the unweighted total $V$, the sum of $v$ over the same
+ballots. The outcome among options MUST be decided on $W$. Any quorum, and the
+420,000 ZEC participation threshold of ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016], MUST be measured
+on $V$.
+
+## Excluded coins
+
+Value in the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox [^zip-2001] and the NSM value balance
+[^zip-0237] are chain value pool balances, not outputs or notes. They cannot
+produce lock records and MUST NOT be counted.
+
+## Poll operator obligations
+
+Before height $S$ the operator MUST publish $S$, $C$, $L$, $f$, the accepted
+evidence classes, and the format of $M$. The operator SHOULD NOT verify
+Class T evidence until the block at height $S$ has at least 100
+confirmations. After the poll the operator MUST publish $W$ and $V$ for every
+option and SHOULD publish only totals. Operators MAY rehearse on Testnet,
+where Mainnet thresholds do not apply.
+
+
+# Security Considerations
+
+**Borrow-to-vote.** Borrow ZEC, lock it, vote, repay after unlock. At an
+annual borrowing cost $r$, a one-week unlocked borrow costs about $r/52$ of
+$v$ for weight $0.1\,v$; a lock of $L$ costs about $4r$ of $v$ for weight $v$,
+roughly twenty times more per unit of weight, and the loan must run until
+$u$.
+
+**Lock-and-hedge.** Lock $v$ and short $v$ elsewhere, voting with no net
+exposure. This costs funding and margin over $\ell$ and remains possible; the
+design raises cost, it does not make this impossible.
+
+**Splitting.** Because $m$ is linear below the cap, weight per ZEC-block is
+constant, so no partition of a holding across lock lengths changes its total
+weight.
+
+**Last-minute locks.** A lock placed the day before $S$ that reaches past $L$
+counts in full. The forward commitment is the same whenever the lock was
+placed; what such a voter lacks is past holding, which this ZIP does not
+weigh. See [Open questions].
+
+**Vote buying** is unchanged in kind. A seller must lock to sell full weight,
+so the price rises, but the trade exists.
+
+**Custodians.** A custodian that owes coins on demand cannot lock them without
+a liquidity mismatch, so voting customer coins at full weight gets harder.
+That is intended. The limits: a custodian can lock its own float or accept
+the mismatch, and this ZIP does not verify custody.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+*Amount only (status quo).* One ZEC, one vote, movable right after the
+snapshot [^forum-nu7-vote]. The vote can be rented for a week's exposure.
+
+*One person, one vote.* Zcash has no sybil-resistant identity. The Zcash
+Community Advisory Panel already gives a per-person signal alongside
+coinholder polls [^zfnd-nu7-results].
+
+*Square root or logarithm of amount.* Without identity, any concave function
+of amount is defeated by splitting a holding across ballots.
+
+*Conviction tiers* [^polkadot-opengov]. Multipliers that step with lock
+length let a holder pick the best point on the curve by splitting. Linear with
+a cap, as in Curve's vote-escrow [^curve-vecrv], does not.
+
+*Age weighting.* Weight by how long coins have already been held. For
+shielded notes this is provable today without a consensus change: the note
+commitment tree is append-only, so a note's position bounds its creation
+height, and the proof-of-balance draft [^draft-str4d-balance-proof] already
+proves holding at a snapshot. In the *Ironwood pool*, age is bounded by the
+pool's activation in July 2026 [^zip-0258] and reset by migration
+[^zip-0318]. It is backward-looking, so it does not express willingness to
+stay, but it defeats buy-vote-sell and last-minute locks directly. Not
+adopted here; see [Open questions].
+
+*Time-averaged balance.* Several snapshots, several proofs per ballot, still
+passive. A forward lock supplies its own window.
+
+## Rationale for the cap and floor
+
+The cap is one halving interval: the longest horizon over which the protocol
+itself plans issuance, and the four-year maximum of vote-escrow systems
+[^curve-vecrv]. The floor is non-zero so that this ZIP does not change who
+can vote; zero would exclude every shielded holder until Class S exists. One
+tenth is the weight of an unlocked vote in Polkadot's conviction voting
+[^polkadot-opengov].
+
+## Rationale for measuring in blocks
+
+`OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY` heights are blocks, and NU7 cuts the target spacing
+from 75 to 25 seconds [^zip-0218], so a lock expressed in time would change
+meaning at activation. Measuring $\ell$ and $L$ in blocks at height $S$ keeps
+the weight well defined.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* Will any poll operator add a Class T path to a shielded-only mechanism, and
+  what is $M$ there?
+* Should past holding (age) count toward $\ell$, generally or as the shielded
+  interim before Class S?
+* Are $f = 1/10$ and $L$ = one halving interval right? Should $f$ drop to
+  zero once Class S exists?
+* Should a lock have to reach past a fixed horizon rather than only past $C$?
+* Should Coinholder-Controlled Fund coins held by the Key-Holder
+  Organizations [^zip-0271] be excluded? ZIP 1016 restricts no one.
+* Should Class T accept time-form or `OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY` locks
+  (ZIP 112 [^zip-0112])?
+* ZIP 1016 decides on ZEC cast in favour and, between competing grants, on
+  ZEC committed in support. Deciding on $W$ changes that; applying this ZIP
+  to ZIP 1016 votes needs its Owners and an Updates header.
+* Which network upgrade could carry Class S? `[VERIFY: NU8 planning]`
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+This ZIP applies to a poll when the operator announces, before $S$, that the
+poll follows it. Class T is usable once an operator implements its
+verification. Class S is usable only after its consensus ZIP activates on
+Mainnet; until then, shielded coins vote under Class H at the floor weight.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+

+

prs.bodyExcerpt: [Rendered.](https://github.com/upbqdn/zips/blob/10s-block-target-spacing/zips/draft-marek-10s-block-target-spacing.md) Proposes reducing the block target spacing from 25 seconds (ZIP 218, NU7) to 10 seconds in NU8. The change is limited to latency. The block subsidy, halving interval, funding-stream

@@ -0,0 +1,279 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: 10-second Block Target Spacing
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Consensus
+    Created: 2026-10-31
+    License: MIT
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "SHALL", "SHOULD", and "SHOULD NOT" in this document are
+to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they
+appear in all capitals.
+
+The term "network upgrade" is to be interpreted as defined in ZIP 200.
+[^zip-0200]
+
+The term "block target spacing" is to be interpreted as defined in ZIP 218.
+[^zip-0218]
+
+The character § is used when referring to sections of the Zcash Protocol
+Specification. [^protocol]
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in
+§ 3.12 'Mainnet and Testnet'. [^protocol-networks]
+
+"NU8" is the code name of the network upgrade that deploys this proposal.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This proposal changes the block target spacing from 25 seconds to 10 seconds
+in NU8. The block subsidy, the block size limit, and the shielded action limits
+of each block are scaled by the same factor, so that issuance, block space, and
+shielded capacity per unit of time are unchanged.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 218 reduces the block target spacing from 75 seconds to 25 seconds in NU7
+in order to reduce transaction latency. [^zip-0218] This proposal reduces it to
+10 seconds, which reduces the expected time to a first confirmation from 25
+seconds to 10 seconds.
+
+The proposal changes latency only. Each quantity that NU7 specifies per unit of
+time is preserved: issuance, funding stream address periods, reissuance by the
+Network Sustainability Mechanism, the duration of the difficulty averaging
+window, and the resource limits of the block chain.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+The changes below are made to the Zcash Protocol Specification [^protocol] and
+to ZIPs 207, 214, and 237 [^zip-0207] [^zip-0214] [^zip-0237], as amended for
+NU7 by ZIP 218 [^zip-0218] and ZIP 259 [^zip-0259].
+
+## Block target spacing
+
+In § 5.3 'Constants' [^protocol-constants], define:
+
+$$\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight} : \mathbb{N}$$
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing} : \mathbb{N} := 10 \textsf{ seconds}$$
+
+In § 7.7.3 'Difficulty adjustment' [^protocol-diffadjustment], define:
+
+$$\mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} : \mathbb{Q} := \mathsf{PostNU7PoWTargetSpacing} \;/\; \mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing} = 5/2$$
+
+$$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated} : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathsf{false}, \mathsf{true}\}$$
+$$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height}) := (\mathsf{height} \geq \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight})$$
+
+On each network, $\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$ SHALL be even.
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{PoWTargetSpacing}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case
+$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing}$ "otherwise".
+
+## Difficulty averaging window
+
+In § 5.3 'Constants', define:
+
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWAveragingWindow} : \mathbb{N} := 255$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{PoWAveragingWindow}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case
+$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWAveragingWindow}$ "otherwise".
+
+The averaging window timespan therefore remains 2,550 seconds.
+
+## Halving interval and block subsidy
+
+Define:
+
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval} : \mathbb{N} := \mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval} \cdot \mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} = 12{,}600{,}000$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{Halving}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\left\lfloor \dfrac{\mathsf{BlossomActivationHeight} - \mathsf{SlowStartShift}}{\mathsf{PreBlossomHalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{NU7ActivationHeight} - \mathsf{BlossomActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostBlossomHalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight} - \mathsf{NU7ActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{height} - \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval}} \right\rfloor,
+  \quad \textsf{otherwise}
+$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{ScheduledBlockSubsidy}$ in ZIP 237, replace the
+condition "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$" of the case added by
+ZIP 218 with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\mathsf{floor}\left(\dfrac{\mathsf{MaxBlockSubsidy}}{\mathsf{BlossomPoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot \mathsf{NU7PoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot \mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot 2^{\mathsf{Halving}(\mathsf{height})}}\right),
+  \quad \textsf{if } \mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})
+$$
+
+The denominator is $15 \cdot 2^{\mathsf{Halving}(\mathsf{height})}$.
+
+## Block size and shielded action limits
+
+For a block at a height for which $\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$,
+the size of the block MUST be less than or equal to 800,000 bytes, in place of
+the limit of 2,000,000 bytes in § 7.6 'Block Header Encoding and Consensus'.
+[^protocol-blockheader]
+
+For such a block, the shielded action limits of ZIP 218 apply with
+$\mathsf{GlobalShieldedBudget} = 132$,
+$\mathsf{OrchardProtocolBlockActionLimit} = 132$, and
+$\mathsf{SaplingBlockIOLimit} = 120$. $\mathsf{SproutBlockJoinSplitLimit}$
+remains 0.
+
+## Funding streams
+
+Let $A$, $R$, $C$, $I$, and $H_1$ be as in the definition of
+$\mathsf{AddressPeriod}$ in Revision 2 of ZIP 207, and let
+$B = \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$. In that definition, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\mathsf{floor}\left(\dfrac{5\left(R(A + I - H_1) + B - A\right) + 2(\mathsf{height} - B)}{5RC}\right),
+  \quad \textsf{otherwise}
+$$
+
+This preserves the address index at NU8 activation. Each later address period
+lasts $5RC/2 = 262{,}500$ blocks.
+
+For each funding stream that is active at $B$ and whose end height is
+$\mathsf{HeightForHalving}(3)$ by Revision 3 of ZIP 214, the end height SHALL
+be $\mathsf{HeightForHalving}(3)$ calculated using the $\mathsf{Halving}$
+function of this proposal. If $H_3$ is the third-halving height under ZIP 218
+(6,132,390 on Mainnet and 4,497,948 on Testnet), this end height is
+$B + 5(H_3 - B)/2$. The number of addresses that ZIP 207 requires
+for each such stream is unchanged.
+
+## Network Sustainability Mechanism
+
+In ZIP 237, $\mathsf{HalvingInterval}(\mathsf{height})$ is
+$\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval}$ if $\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$.
+From NU8 activation, $\mathsf{BLOCK\_SUBSIDY\_FRACTION}$ is therefore
+$550 / 10^{10}$.
+
+If $B$ is less than the $\mathsf{DEPLOYMENT\_BLOCK\_HEIGHT}$ that ZIP 237
+specifies for a network, then $\mathsf{DEPLOYMENT\_BLOCK\_HEIGHT}$ for that
+network SHALL instead be calculated as in ZIP 237, with $B$ in place of $A$,
+with $\mathsf{ScheduledBlockSubsidy}$, $H_3$, and $H_4$ as specified by this
+proposal, and with 550 in place of 1375. NU8 activation heights SHALL be chosen
+so that this height exists before $H_4$. The NU8 deployment ZIP specifies the
+resulting height for each network.
+
+## Minimum-difficulty blocks on Testnet
+
+On Testnet, from NU8 activation, the minimum-difficulty threshold specified by
+ZIP 218 is $45 \cdot \mathsf{PoWTargetSpacing}(\mathsf{height})$ seconds, which
+remains 450 seconds.
+
+## Unchanged consensus rules
+
+Consensus rules that are expressed in blocks and not changed above, including
+the coinbase maturity of 100 blocks and $\mathsf{PoWMedianBlockSpan}$, are
+unchanged.
+
+## Non-consensus changes
+
+From NU8 activation:
+
+- Wallets SHOULD use a default expiry delta of 300 blocks, in place of the 120
+  blocks recommended by ZIP 218.
+- Nodes SHOULD support rolling back at least 1,500 blocks, in place of the 600
+  blocks recommended by ZIP 218.
+- Implementations SHOULD multiply the block-count constants that ZIP 218
+  multiplies by 3 by $\mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio}$, rounding up.
+- Nodes SHOULD NOT admit to their mempools or relay, and wallets SHOULD NOT
+  create, a transaction that alone exceeds the block size or shielded action
+  limits above.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+A target spacing of 10 seconds makes each scaled quantity an integer: the
+averaging window of 255 blocks, the halving interval of 12,600,000 blocks, the
+address period of 262,500 blocks, and the limits of 800,000 bytes, 132
+actions, and 120 Sapling inputs and outputs.
+
+Every post-NU7 halving height is even on both networks. An even activation
+height $B$ therefore maps each such height $H$ to the integer height
+$B + 5(H - B)/2$, so that no halving boundary falls within a 25-second block.
+
+Scaling the per-block limits by 2/5 keeps the worst-case validation work,
+compact sync bandwidth, and chain growth per unit of time at their NU7 values.
+ZIP 218 bounds worst-case compact sync bandwidth at 169.10 MB per day.
+[^zip-0218] Without the scaling, each of these would increase by a factor of
+5/2.
+
+The post-NU8 block subsidy differs from 2/5 of the post-NU7 block subsidy by
+less than one zatoshi, due to rounding. If NU8 activates before the third
+halving, this reduces total scheduled issuance, relative to ZIP 218, by
+$(H_3 - B)/2$ zatoshi before the third halving and by 1.134 ZEC after it.
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+The stale block rate increases with the ratio of block propagation time to the
+block target spacing. ZIP 218 reports a stale block rate of 4.86% for 2 MB
+blocks at 25-second spacing on a 99-node devnet. [^zip-0218] The rate at
+10-second spacing has not been measured; it needs to be measured before
+deployment. Smaller blocks and compact block relay [^draft-compact-block-relay]
+reduce propagation time.
+
+A given number of confirmations corresponds to 2.5 times less time. Where
+propagation time is significant relative to the target spacing, it also
+provides less security against an attacker with a given fraction of the hash
+power.
+
+Wallets that select an anchor three blocks behind the chain tip, as
+recommended by ZIP 315 [^zip-0315], select one about 30 seconds old. A rollback
+past the anchor invalidates the transaction, and links its revealed nullifiers
+to any later transaction that spends the same notes. More frequent blocks also
+give observers finer timing information.
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+This proposal is intended to be deployed in NU8. The NU8 deployment ZIP will
+specify $\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$ for each network.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 or later](protocol/protocol.pdf)
+
+[^protocol-networks]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 3.12: Mainnet and Testnet](protocol/protocol.pdf#networks)
+
+[^protocol-constants]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 5.3: Constants](protocol/protocol.pdf#constants)
+
+[^protocol-blockheader]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 7.6: Block Header Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockheader)
+
+[^protocol-diffadjustment]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 7.7.3: Difficulty adjustment](protocol/protocol.pdf#diffadjustment)
+
+[^zip-0200]: [ZIP 200: Network Upgrade Mechanism](zip-0200.rst)
+
+[^zip-0207]: [ZIP 207: Funding Streams](zip-0207.rst)
+
+[^zip-0214]: [ZIP 214: Consensus rules for a Zcash Development Fund](zip-0214.rst)
+
+[^zip-0218]: [ZIP 218: 25-second Block Target Spacing](zip-0218.md)
+
+[^zip-0237]: [ZIP 237: Network Sustainability Mechanism: Halving-Preserving Issuance](zip-0237.md)
+
+[^zip-0259]: [ZIP 259: Deployment of the NU7 Network Upgrade](zip-0259.md)
+
+[^zip-0315]: [ZIP 315: Best Practices for Wallet Implementations](zip-0315.rst)
+
+[^draft-compact-block-relay]: [Draft ZIP: Compact Block Relay](https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1429)
